item.title: Germany backs Ukraine's Zelenskiy after Trump's call for his removal
item.description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks. Wadephul said Germany remained by the side of Ukraine and its government "and fully support the President as he carries out his difficult duties." The comments, at a leadership meeting of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), followed Trump's call on Saturday for Zelenskiy to be replaced and underlined Berlin's growing rift with Washington. Trump, who last week announced a diesel supply deal with Russia, called for Ukraine to [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"replace Zelenskiy"] and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure. Germany, the biggest European donor to Ukraine, said on Saturday it would [USN:L1N45W02N TEXT:"maintain sanctions"] against Russia despite Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel. Wadephul, who met his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month, said "consistency and clarity" were needed to support Ukraine and bring Moscow to negotiate. "We don't need less pressure, we need more pressure on Putin to make him be ready to negotiate," Wadephul said. "That is what this moment requires and that's what the government stands for." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskiy [USN:FWN45V15A TEXT:"on Saturday"] and told him the UK would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia, a Downing Street spokesperson said.

item.title: Deutsche Bank chief warns German election results worrying foreign investors
item.description: The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes. The AfD, which wants to restrict immigration and send asylum seekers home, scored some of its biggest-ever wins in eastern Germany last month. At the same time, the Left Party scored its biggest win in the election for the city government of Berlin, pledging to [USN:L1N45C05W TEXT:"expropriate holdings"] of property companies. "This poses a significant risk to Germany, and it should not be played down," Christian Sewing, chief executive of Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) , told the Bild daily in an interview, referring to the rise of political extremes. "You can't expect a foreign investor to immediately draw a distinction between a state government and Germany as a whole," he said. "It's seen as Germany as a whole and I think that from an investor's point of view, that's understandable." In the state of Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD, which is classified by security services as extremist in some regions, only narrowly fell short of an [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"absolute majority"] in the state parliament, and it followed up two weeks later by taking first place in [USN:L1N45C01D TEXT:"Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania"]. The AfD has been accused by economists of fostering a climate that will drive away badly needed skilled workers and foreign investors. The Left Party, meanwhile, vowed to tackle Berlin's soaring housing costs by [USN:L8N45D1DV TEXT:"expropriating the holdings"] of residential property companies. "And whether it's Saxony-Anhalt with the AfD or what's happening here in Berlin, it's anything but conducive to economic growth. And it's anything but investment-friendly," Sewing said. He urged the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz to carry on with reforms to revive the economy. "That is the only response we have to the far-right and far-left extremists in this country," he said.

item.title: Zelenski dice que Ucrania cesará ataques a refinerías si Rusia deja en paz su sistema de energía
item.description: Ucrania está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas si Moscú pone fin al bombardeo de la infraestructura energética ucraniana, dijo el domingo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, exigió a Kiev un cese unilateral.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ucrania está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas si Moscú pone fin al bombardeo de la infraestructura energética ucraniana, dijo el domingo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, exigió a Kiev un cese unilateral. Trump culpó el sábado a los ataques ucranianos contra las refinerías rusas del aumento de los precios del diésel en Estados Unidos y dijo que a Zelenski "más le vale dejar de hacerlo", además sostuvo que Ucrania debería sustituirlo como líder porque había desperdiciado varias oportunidades para llegar a un acuerdo con Moscú. La fuerte subida de los precios mundiales del diésel, tras el estallido de la guerra de Irán en febrero, se ha convertido en un lastre político para el Partido Republicano de Trump antes de las elecciones legislativas del próximo mes, en las que los demócratas de la oposición podrían hacerse con el control de una o ambas cámaras del Congreso. Zelenski reiteró el domingo la postura que Ucrania mantiene desde hace tiempo: que está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías rusas únicamente como parte de una desescalada mutua del conflicto, lo que requeriría que Moscú cese sus propios ataques contra las infraestructuras energéticas ucranianas. Cualquier acuerdo de este tipo tendría que ir acompañado de "garantías reales", dijo Zelenskiy. "La verdadera causa de la guerra en Europa es Rusia y solo Rusia", dijo Zelenskiy, sin aludir específicamente a las declaraciones de Trump. "Es posible detener los ataques contra las infraestructuras energéticas ya desde hoy mismo, pero Putin no quiere hacerlo". El sábado, Zelenski respondió airadamente al anuncio de Trump sobre un acuerdo de suministro de gasóleo con Rusia, que, según él, alentaría los ataques de Moscú contra Ucrania. Analistas dijeron que es poco probable que el acuerdo de Trump con Moscú resulte en una baja sostenida de los precios del combustible, ya que los volúmenes siguen siendo muy inferiores a los que Rusia suele exportar cuando sus refinerías no están bajo ataque. El acuerdo sobre el gasóleo también fue criticado por legisladores estadounidenses, entre ellos uno de los compañeros republicanos de Trump, el diputado Don Bacon, quien dijo que era el momento de aplicar más sanciones, no de levantarlas. En las calles de Kiev, varios residentes expresaron su indignación ante la sugerencia de Trump de que Ucrania debería buscar un nuevo líder dispuesto a llegar a un acuerdo con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin. "Nadie tiene derecho a decirnos qué hacer, sobre todo porque no se pueden tener elecciones en tiempo de guerra", dijo Sabina, una profesora de primaria de 40 años, refiriéndose a la prohibición de comicios en Ucrania bajo la ley marcial por razones de seguridad. "En mi opinión, es una traición por parte de nuestros socios", añadió sobre las declaraciones de Trump.

WARSAW: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday (Oct 11) after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said. Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not go into details but authorities were treating the threat as "deadly serious". "We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out," he told reporters. Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security. While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians. In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

Source: Reuters/cy

item.title: Mueren 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, en naufragio entre Yibuti a Yemen: agencia de la ONU
item.description: Al menos 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, fallecieron y más de 116 están desaparecidos tras el naufragio de una embarcación que transportaba a unas 305 personas desde Yibuti a Yemen, informó el domingo la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) de las Naciones Unidas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Al menos 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, fallecieron y más de 116 están desaparecidos tras el naufragio de una embarcación que transportaba a unas 305 personas desde Yibuti a Yemen, informó el domingo la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) de las Naciones Unidas. La embarcación zozobró cerca de Guhere, al norte de la ciudad portuaria yibutiana de Obock, durante la noche del 8 al 9 de octubre, según la OIM, que recabó testimonios de los supervivientes. Más de 80 personas sobrevivieron al naufragio, todas ellas de nacionalidad etíope, según el comunicado. Un portavoz del Gobierno etíope no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. De los 109 cadáveres recuperados tras el naufragio, 52 son hombres, 42 mujeres y 15 niños, según la OIM. "Nuestros equipos se encuentran sobre el terreno junto a las autoridades locales para prestar asistencia de emergencia", dijo Alexandre Coissac, jefe de misión de la OIM en Yibuti. "Esta tragedia es un claro recordatorio de los peligros a los que se enfrentan los migrantes en este corredor migratorio en su búsqueda de oportunidades económicas", añadió Coissac. Las autoridades de Yibuti continúan con las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, según el comunicado de la OIM, que añadió que las autoridades locales también están prestando asistencia médica a los supervivientes y organizando los entierros de los fallecidos. No fue posible contactar de inmediato con el Gobierno de Yibuti para recabar sus comentarios. Yemen está viviendo la escalada más grave de los combates entre las fuerzas gubernamentales respaldadas por Arabia Saudita y los hutíes, apoyados por Irán, desde que una tregua negociada por la ONU detuvo en gran medida los ataques transfronterizos en 2022. La reanudación del conflicto podría redefinir el control en Yemen, con repercusiones para las rutas marítimas del mar Rojo. La OIM calificó de alarmante la crisis desencadenada por los combates, con cifras de desplazados que se han disparado de 76 000 a 200 000 desde mediados de septiembre, según datos publicados por la OIM la semana pasada. Más de 3.700 personas han huido de Yemen por mar hacia Yibuti hasta la semana pasada, según la OIM. El mes pasado también estallaron combates en Etiopía, en lo que supone la mayor escalada de violencia desde la guerra de Tigray.

item.title: Simón se convertirá en un huracán muy intenso frente al Pacífico mexicano, según las previsiones
item.description: El huracán Simón se convertirá en uno de gran intensidad el domingo, cerca de la costa centrooccidental de México, y se acercará mucho a la ribera el lunes, pronosticó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (CNH) de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Simón se convertirá en uno de gran intensidad el domingo, cerca de la costa centrooccidental de México, y se acercará mucho a la ribera el lunes, pronosticó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (CNH) de Estados Unidos. Simon se encontraba a unos 96.56 kilometros al oeste suroeste de Manzanillo a primera hora de la mañana del domingo, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 250 kilómetros, según la última actualización del CNH.

item.title: Arsenal forward Russo voted as England women's player of the year
item.description: Forward Alessia Russo has been voted by fans as England women's player of the year for the 2025-26 season, winning the award for the second time in her career, the national team announced on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Forward Alessia Russo has been voted by fans as England women's player of the year for the 2025-26 season, winning the award for the second time in her career, the national team announced on Sunday. Arsenal player Russo, who also won the award in 2023-24, was the most prolific English scorer in the Women's Super League last season with 13 goals and six assists. Her double in a 3-0 win over Aston Villa in May helped Arsenal secure Champions League qualification. The 27-year-old also played a leading role in England's World Cup qualification campaign, starting in all six group matches and scoring three times. "To receive the award is really special, particularly as it comes directly from the fans," said Russo, who beat Lucy Bronze and Hannah Hampton in the poll. "I absolutely love playing for England every moment I get... hopefully we will go on to have a really big season." Russo was on the scoresheet when England beat Greece 3-1 in their World Cup round one playoff tie on Friday, with the reverse fixture set for Tuesday in Leicester.

item.title: Le pape Léon va être opéré d'un nodule au poumon
item.description: Le pape Léon a déclaré dimanche que les médecins avaient détecté une petite excroissance pulmonaire lors d'un récent examen de santé et qu'il subirait une intervention chirurgicale cette semaine pour la retirer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le pape Léon a déclaré dimanche que les médecins avaient détecté une petite excroissance pulmonaire lors d'un récent examen de santé et qu'il subirait une intervention chirurgicale cette semaine pour la retirer. Âgé de 71 ans, Léon a déclaré aux pèlerins réunis sur la place Saint-Pierre à l'occasion de sa prière dominicale hebdomadaire que cette excroissance était circonscrite et avait été détectée à un stade précoce. "Récemment, à l'occasion de certains examens, les médecins ont trouvé un nodule circonscrit au poumon. Il a été détecté à un stade très précoce et est bien localisé", a déclaré le souverain pontife. "Les médecins estiment qu'il convient d'intervenir et, suivant leurs conseils, j'ai décidé de subir une intervention chirurgicale pour le retirer", a-t-il déclaré. "Cette intervention est déjà programmée dans les prochains jours." Le bureau de presse du Vatican a précisé que la convalescence du pape après l'opération devrait durer environ une semaine.

item.title: El papa León se someterá a una cirugía para extirpar un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón
item.description: El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo. León, de 71 años, explicó a los peregrinos reunidos en la Plaza de San Pedro para su oración dominical semanal que el nódulo estaba "bien localizado" y se había detectado a tiempo, y les pidió que oraran "por la visita pastoral que voy a realizar" a Uruguay, Argentina y Perú. "Recientemente, durante unos exámenes médicos, los médicos encontraron un nódulo localizado en mi pulmón", dijo el pontífice. "Se detectó en una fase muy temprana y está bien localizado". "Los médicos consideran aconsejable intervenir, por lo que, siguiendo su consejo, he decidido someterme a una intervención quirúrgica para extirparlo", añadió. "La operación ya está programada para los próximos días". Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. Según la Sociedad Torácica Americana, menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores. Leo, elegido papa por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es más joven de lo usual para ser jefe de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, entre ellos el tenis, y no se tiene constancia de que haya tenido problemas de salud antes. Su predecesor, el difunto papa Francisco, falleció a los 88 años y se encontraba cada vez más débil en sus últimos años. La oficina de prensa del Vaticano indicó que se esperaba que la recuperación de Leo tras la intervención quirúrgica durara aproximadamente una semana. No facilitó de inmediato más detalles sobre el estado de salud del papa. Leo tiene una agenda muy apretada y tiene previsto realizar una gira de 11 días por Uruguay, Argentina y Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre.

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo said on Sunday (Oct 11) that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. Pope Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. "Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localised nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."

"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days." A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5 per cent of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size and other factors such as smoking. Pope Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well. "I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement. "The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it during today’s Angelus are reassuring," Meloni added. The late Pope Francis, Pope Leo's predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years. The Vatican press office said the pope's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health. Pope Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17. Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake".

VATICAN CITY, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff’s tenure.

Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter’s Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was “well-contained” and caught at an early stage.

“Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung,” said the pontiff. “It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained.”

“The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it,” he said. “The operation is already scheduled for the next few days.”

The late Pope Francis, Leo’s predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.

The Vatican press office said Leo’s recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope’s health.

item.title: ローマ教皇、肺に小さなしこり 数日以内に手術へ
item.description: [バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] - ローマ教皇レオ１４世（７１）は１２日、先の健康診断で肺に小さなしこりが見つかり、今週中に切除手術を受けると明らかにした。２０２５年５月の就任後、健康問題が明らかになるのは初めて。

バチカンのサンピエトロ広場で行った日曜恒例の祈りの集いで信者らに説明した。しこりは局所的なもので、ごく早期に発見されたという。

教皇は「（医師の）助言に従い、切除手術を受けることを決めた」と述べた。手術は数日以内に予定されているという。

レオ１４世は７１歳と教皇としては比較的若く、テニスなどのスポーツを好む。これまで大きな健康問題は知られていなかった。前任のフランシスコ教皇は晩年、健康状態が悪化し、８８歳で死去した。

バチカン報道官室によると、レオ１４世は術後１週間程度で回復する見通し。健康状態について、それ以上の詳細は明らかにしていない。

item.content:encoded: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. "Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained." "The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days." A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking. "Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. "When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said. LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well. "I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement. "The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added. The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health. The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health. Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17. Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

WARSAW, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, an Interior Ministry spokesperson said on X.

The exact nature of the threat and its origin were not immediately clear.

“Following information received by the Polish Police regarding a possible attack …Interior Minister, Marcin Kierwiński, and the Minister-Coordinator of Special Services, Tomasz Siemoniak, have ordered action to be taken in this matter,” spokesperson Karolina Galecka wrote.

Show Full Article

“A meeting will be held today at 11:00 a.m. at the Internal Security Agency’s Counter-Terrorism Centre.”

A spokesperson for the minister-coordinator of special services said he had no further comment.

Private broadcaster Radio Zet reported that police had received an email with information about the threat.

While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.

In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.

In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

Sunday’s announcement came as authorities in Poland have been on high alert following a wave of violence in schools that resulted in the death of a caretaker on Thursday.

(Reporting by Alan CharlishEditing by Tomasz Janowski and Christina Fincher)

item.title: フーシ派、サウジ空港・領空は「作戦区域」 軍事作戦に報復警告
item.description:
Jana Choukeir Maha El Dahan Timour Azhari
［ドバイ／リヤド １１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jana Choukeir　Maha El Dahan　Timour Azhari

［ドバイ／リヤド　１１日　ロイター］ - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１１日、航空会社や旅行者、空港関係者に対し、サウジアラビア国内の空港に近づかないよう警告した。サウジがイエメンで軍事行動を続ければ、さらに強い対応を招くと主張した。

１０日には首都リヤドの国際空港が攻撃を受け、少なくとも１２人が死亡し、３００人余りが負傷。トランプ米大統領は、サウジの対フーシ派軍事作戦に参加するか「検討」する考えを示した。

フーシ派はＸへの投稿で「全ての航空会社、専門家、従業員、労働者、旅行者に対し、サウジの空港と領空を使用しないよう改めて警告する。（聖地である）メッカとメディナの空港を除き、サウジの空港と領空は攻撃に対して脆弱（ぜいじゃく）であり、われわれの作戦部隊の作戦区域となっている」と表明。「迎撃に失敗した場合の責任はサウジ側にある」とした。

フーシ派の「外務省」は１１日、「サウジという敵がイエメンへの侵略と干渉をやめなければ、さらに悪い事態が訪れるだろう」と述べた。フーシ派系メディアが伝えた。

１０日のリヤドの空港に対する攻撃は過去１週間で３回目。死者は、サウジ人が４人、バングラデシュ人２人のほか、米国、ヨルダン、パレスチナ、シリア、スーダン、エジプト国籍の人が含まれている。

航空当局は、被害状況と安全性の評価を行うため空港業務を一時停止したと発表した。再開時期は示していない。

サウジ主導の連合軍は１０日、サウジ東部ダンマームのキング・ファハド国際空港付近にも飛翔体が落下したと発表した。１１日も同地域で無人機（ドローン）１機を迎撃したと明らかにした。

サウジのエネルギー省は、世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は予定通り１１日からリヤドで開催されると発表した。この会合は空港から約１０キロメートルの施設で１１─１５日の日程で開催される。国営テレビによると、閣僚７０人以上、企業幹部３００人、国際エネルギー機関２５団体以上の代表者が出席する予定だ。

item.title: 109 migrants, including 15 children dead after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
item.description: At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, have died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying about 305 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, have died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying about 305 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday. The boat capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of 8–9 October, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts. More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals, the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Among the 109 bodies recovered after the boat capsized, 52 are men, 42 women and 15 children including nine girls and six boys, the IOM said. "Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac. "This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said. Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased. The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment. Yemen is [USN:L6N45T0PU TEXT:"experiencing"] the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. The renewed conflict could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes. IOM described the crisis sparked by the fighting as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the IOM last week. More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, according to the IOM. Fighting also broke out in Ethiopia last month in the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis renew warning over Saudi airports after deadly Riyadh attack
item.description: The deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 at Riyadh's international airport.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis warned airlines, travellers and airport workers on Sunday to stay away from Saudi airports, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"12 people"] and wounded more than 300 others. It was the deadliest such attack in the kingdom in more than a decade and comes amid an escalation of [USN:S8N43806H TEXT:"fighting"] between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. "We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces, with the exception of the airports in (the holy cities of) Mecca and Medina," the Houthis said in a post on X. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions." Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month. Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said on Sunday that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity. "Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television. President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday that a projectile had also fallen near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The coalition also reported intercepting a drone in the region on Sunday. INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD IN RIYADH Saturday's attack has forced the temporary closure of King Khalid International Airport but the Saudi energy ministry said a long-planned international energy conference was still going ahead in Riyadh on Sunday. The five-day WPC Energy Congress is taking place at a convention centre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport. State TV said more than 70 ministers, 300 company executives and representatives of over 25 international energy organisations have confirmed their attendance. It was not immediately clear whether the participants would attend in person or virtually. A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum is also set to go ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available. Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff. In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the 12 dead included 4 Saudis, 2 Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said airport operations were temporarily suspended pending damage and safety assessments, without specifying when flights would resume. Two previous attacks on Riyadh's international airport earlier in the week had killed four people and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

item.title: Smith sets new catching record as Australia take firm grip on test
item.description: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side took a firm grip on the first test with hosts South Africa 238 runs for eight wickets, still trailing the tourists by 152 runs at tea on the third day at Kingsmead.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side took a firm grip on the first test with hosts South Africa 238 runs for eight wickets, still trailing the tourists by 152 runs at tea on the third day at Kingsmead. Smith took three superb catches on Sunday to take his test tally to 222, going past the record of 220 held by England's Joe Root. Two of the catches showed outstanding anticipation as Smith shuffled across a few steps to snag South Africa captain Temba Bavuma and Kyle Verreynne as they both tried reverse sweeps off the spin bowling of Nathan Lyon, and he also produced a flying dive across first slip to break the record and see off the threat of David Bedingham. Australia captain Pat Cummins took 3-54 to lead a combined bowling effort as South Africa's batsmen were guilty of playing loose shots at crucial junctures of the contest with three wickets falling before lunch and four more in the second session. South Africa added 57 runs to their overnight tally of 27-1 before Aiden Markram got a healthy edge as he tried to drive Mitch Starc and was caught by Matt Renshaw at first slip for 37. An injudicious reverse sweep by Bavuma saw him go cheaply for three runs while Bedingham was out for 49, caught in spectacular fashion by Smith as he edged a back-foot drive. After lunch, Cummins took two quick wickets with Wiaan Mulder (30) out to a miscued hook shot and Tristan Stubbs (32) following shortly as his pulled effort was caught at deep fine leg. Marco Jansen and Verreynne went on the charge when they came to the wicket and both hit lusty blows, but a partnership of 35 runs from 34 balls was ended by Smith’s one-handed catch that saw Verreynne out for 13. Jansen (26 off 20 balls) perished three balls later, when he miscued the ball to be caught at mid-off with South Africa 197-8. Simon Harmer (17 not out) and Keshav Maharaj (23 not out) were offering some late resistance for South Africa in an unbeaten 41-run partnership for the ninth wicket and will resume batting for the final session. The opening two days of the test both ended early when bad light stopped play and extra time has been added on to all three of Sunday's sessions.

item.title: Indonesia moves 8 endangered orangutans to safety after Borneo fires
item.description: Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday. The Southeast Asian nation is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, mainly on Sumatra and Borneo islands, and the government has warned the blazes could continue until November, aggravated by the El Niño weather pattern. Three mother-child pairs and two adolescent male orangutans were among those rescued between August and September from several locations, the Indonesian government and wildlife foundation, Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) said in a statement. "Their relocation to Batu Nyambu protected forest is expected to give the eight orangutans a chance to return to living naturally," the statement read. Orangutans are critically endangered great apes found in the wild only on the Southeast Asian islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with Indonesia home to all three recognised species, according to the World Wildlife Fund. Populations have declined due to deforestation, wildfires and poaching. The relocation operation took six hours by car, one hour on boats, and two more hours on foot, with the orangutans in cages carried on bamboo poles. Before they were moved, YIARI conservationists checked the animals' health. Since August, the West Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency and YIARI have rescued 46 orangutans affected by fires, agency head Murlan Dameria Pane said. From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since. Haze from the fires has caused 175,000 cases of respiratory illness in Indonesia, with the smog affecting neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia where many schools were closed on Friday as air quality deteriorated.

item.title: Kyiv propose à Moscou une désescalade réciproque sur l'énergie
item.description: Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky s'est dit prêt dimanche à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cesse ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que le président américain Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses attaques.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky s'est dit prêt dimanche à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cesse ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que le président américain Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses attaques. Samedi, Donald Trump a imputé la hausse des prix du diesel aux États-Unis aux frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes et a déclaré que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement", ajoutant que l'Ukraine devrait le remplacer à sa tête car il avait laissé passer plusieurs occasions de conclure un accord avec Moscou. La forte hausse des prix mondiaux du diesel, qui a suivi le déclenchement de la guerre avec l'Iran en février, est devenue un handicap politique pour le Parti républicain de Donald Trump à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat du mois prochain, lors desquelles les démocrates pourraient reprendre le contrôle d'une ou des deux chambres du Congrès. Volodimir Zelensky a réaffirmé dimanche la position de longue date de l'Ukraine, selon laquelle elle est disposée à cesser ses attaques contre les raffineries russes uniquement dans le cadre d'une désescalade réciproque du conflit, qui exigerait que Moscou mette également fin à ses frappes contre les infrastructures électriques ukrainiennes. Tout accord de ce type devrait s'accompagner de "garanties réelles", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. "La véritable cause de la guerre en Europe, c'est la Russie et la Russie seule", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky, sans faire directement référence aux propos de Donald Trump. "Il est possible de mettre fin aux frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques dès aujourd'hui, mais Vladimir Poutine ne le veut pas." Samedi, Volodimir Zelensky a réagi avec colère à l'annonce par Donald Trump d'un accord d'approvisionnement en diesel avec la Russie, estimant que celui-ci encouragerait les attaques de Moscou contre l'Ukraine. Des analystes ont déclaré que l'accord conclu par Donald Trump avec Moscou avait peu de chances d'entraîner une baisse durable des prix des carburants, les volumes concernés restant bien inférieurs aux exportations habituelles de la Russie lorsque ses raffineries ne sont pas visées par des attaques. L'accord sur le diesel a également été critiqué par des élus américains, dont le représentant républicain Don Bacon, qui a estimé qu'il était temps de renforcer les sanctions plutôt que de les alléger. Dans les rues de Kyiv, plusieurs habitants ont fait part de leur colère après la suggestion de Donald Trump selon laquelle l'Ukraine devrait se trouver un nouveau dirigeant prêt à conclure un accord avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine. "Personne n'a le droit de nous dire ce que nous devons faire, d'autant que des élections ne peuvent pas être organisées en temps de guerre", a déclaré Sabina, une institutrice de 40 ans, en référence à l'interdiction des élections en Ukraine sous le régime de la loi martiale pour des raisons de sécurité. "À mes yeux, c'est une trahison de la part de nos partenaires", a-t-elle déclaré au sujet des remarques de Donald Trump. Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré qu'il poursuivrait dimanche ses discussions avec les dirigeants européens et que des échanges avaient lieu quotidiennement sur des dispositifs supplémentaires de défense aérienne, notamment des munitions pour les avions de combat utilisés pour abattre les drones russes à réaction. Lundi, le ministre ukrainien des Affaires étrangères, Andriï Sybiha, doit participer à une réunion du Conseil des affaires étrangères de l'Union européenne qui devrait examiner un renforcement de la pression des sanctions contre la Russie ainsi que l'avancement des négociations sur l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Union européenne.

item.title: Ukraine will stop hitting refineries if Russia halts energy attacks, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop its strikes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop its strikes. On Saturday, Trump blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for raising US diesel prices and said Zelenskiy had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""], adding that Ukraine should replace him as leader because he had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow. The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of next month's midterm elections, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress. Zelenskiy on Sunday repeated Ukraine's long-standing position that it was willing to halt attacks on Russian refineries only as part of a mutual de-escalation of the conflict, which would require Moscow to cease its own strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure. Any such deal would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said. "The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said, without alluding specifically to Trump's remarks. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so." On Saturday, Zelenskiy responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, which he said would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine. Analysts said Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices, with the volumes still much lower than what Russia usually exports when its refineries are not under attack. The diesel deal was also criticized by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions, not lift them. On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin. "No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher, referring to Ukraine's [USN:L1N44G089 TEXT:"prohibition on elections under martial law`"] for security reasons. "In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks. Zelenskiy said he would continue discussions with European leaders on Sunday, and there were daily conversations around additional air defence packages, including ammunition for combat aircraft that are used to down Russia's jet-powered drones. On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is due to participate in a European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting that is expected to discuss increasing sanctions pressure on Russia and advancing negotiations on Ukraine’s EU accession.

item.title: Gea sends Shelton crashing out of Shanghai
item.description: US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday. World number four Shelton, who has barely played since losing to Alexander Zverev in September's US Open final and withdrew from the Japan Open due to fitness concerns, lost both sets against the world number 56 in tight tiebreakers. Asked if his recent lack of action had had an effect on him, Shelton told reporters: "I mean, I got outplayed today. The guy played better than me. "A hundred percent, I would have liked to have come over here earlier and be prepared and have already dealt with the jet lag by the time I was playing here in the Shanghai Masters. "My body wasn't ready. I wasn't physically ready to play in Tokyo. That's just the way this tour is sometimes." The 24-year-old American said he was focused on finishing his 2026 campaign on a "high note" at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin next month. "Obviously I want to be prepared and playing some of my best tennis when I get there," he added. "Three tournaments left to finish the year, which has been a very up and down year, but a great year, on a high note." Gea, who next faces either Jakub Mensik or Francisco Cerundolo, was delighted with his first win over a top-10 player. "I'm practicing hard every day since the beginning of the year to win against those guys," he said. "Of course, when you win, it is always special. But, yeah, I was prepared and I was confident before the match. Also playing a really good season right now, so, yeah, that's a really good win, but I was ready for it."

item.title: Hurricane Simon expected to become major hurricane off Mexico coast
item.description: Hurricane Simon is expected to become a major hurricane on Sunday near the west-central coast of Mexico and move very close to the coast on Monday, the US National Hurricane Center said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Simon is expected to become a major hurricane on Sunday near the west-central coast of Mexico and move very close to the coast on Monday, the US National Hurricane Center said. Simon was located about 60 miles (96.56 km) west-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, early Sunday morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 155 mph, NHC said in its latest update.

item.title: Les Houthis renouvellent leurs menaces contre les aéroports saoudiens
item.description: Les Houthis ont renouvelé dimanche leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, au lendemain d'une attaque contre l'aéroport international de Riyad qui a fait 12 morts, appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Les Houthis ont renouvelé dimanche leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, au lendemain d'une attaque contre l'aéroport international de Riyad qui a fait 12 morts, appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés. Le groupe soutenu par l'Iran a déclaré que les aéroports et l'espace aérien saoudiens demeuraient des cibles potentielles d'opérations militaires et a averti que le royaume porterait la responsabilité de toute interception qui échouerait. Ces nouvelles menaces interviennent alors que l'Arabie saoudite a maintenu l'accueil d'un important congrès international de l'énergie à Riyad. Le ministère saoudien de l'Énergie a annoncé que le 25e Congrès mondial de l'énergie (WPC Energy Congress), d'une durée de cinq jours, a débuté dimanche, avec la participation confirmée de plus de 70 ministres, 300 dirigeants d'entreprises et représentants de plus de 25 organisations internationales du secteur de l'énergie, selon la télévision d'État. La réunion ministérielle de l'International Energy Forum devait également se tenir dimanche, sa séance plénière étant organisée à huis clos, selon un avis aux médias. L'attaque de samedi, la troisième visant l'aéroport de Riyad en une semaine, a fait au moins 12 morts et 309 blessés, selon les autorités saoudiennes. Parmi les victimes figurent quatre Saoudiens, deux Bangladais ainsi que des ressortissants des États-Unis, de Jordanie, de Palestine, de Syrie, du Soudan et d'Égypte. L'autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile a déclaré que les opérations de l'aéroport avaient été temporairement suspendues dans l'attente d'évaluations des dégâts et des conditions de sécurité, sans préciser quand les vols reprendraient. L'ambassade des États-Unis à Riyad a exhorté les citoyens américains à éviter l'aéroport et les zones environnantes. Elle a également précisé que les employés du gouvernement américain devaient obtenir une autorisation spéciale pour utiliser les aéroports de Riyad, Djeddah et Dammam. Le président Donald Trump a déclaré samedi que Washington envisageait de se joindre aux frappes saoudiennes contre les Houthis et qu'une décision serait prise rapidement après cette attaque meurtrière.

item.title: INWIT shareholders explore financing for potential take-private deal
item.description: French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone and KKR, are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The leading shareholders in INWIT are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers. French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone and KKR, are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT, the people said. Ardian controls 32% of INWIT, while Oak Holdings controls 39%. The investors are discussing the financing of the bid with banks, the people said, with one person adding that Abu Dhabi investment firm Mubadala is expected to take a stake in INWIT as part of the plan. The people cautioned that deliberations are still ongoing. Ardian, GIP, Vodafone, KKR and Mubadala declined to comment. GIP is part of US investment firm Blackrock . An INWIT spokesperson said the company did not have any information on the matter. INWIT, which listed in Milan in 2015, has been the subject of takeover speculation since a French media report in February that infrastructure fund Ardian and investment group Brookfield were interested in taking the Italian company private. INWIT has since then become embroiled in a dispute with its two main customers, Telecom Italia (TIM) and Swisscom's Fastweb, both of which have initiated procedures to terminate their respective contracts with INWIT as part of efforts to renegotiate them on more favourable terms. INWIT's market value has fallen about 27% over the past year to $7.1 billion (€6.3 billion) as of Friday's close, according to LSEG data.

Ardian controls 32% of INWIT, while Oak Holdings controls 39%. The investors are discussing the financing of the bid with banks, the people said, with one person adding that Abu Dhabi investment firm Mubadala is expected to take a stake in INWIT as part of the plan. The people cautioned that deliberations are still ongoing. Ardian, GIP, Vodafone (VOD.L) , KKR (KKR.N) and Mubadala declined to comment. GIP is part of US investment firm Blackrock (BLK.N) . An INWIT spokesperson said the company did not have any information on the matter. INWIT has since then become [USN:L8N43G1LQ TEXT:"embroiled in a dispute"] with its two main customers, Telecom Italia (TIM) (TLIT.MI) and Swisscom's Fastweb (SCMN.S) , both of which have initiated procedures to terminate their respective contracts with INWIT as part of efforts to renegotiate them on more favourable terms. item.title: Polish security services meet after 'serious' threat to PM and defence minister
item.description: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said. Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not go into details but authorities were treating the threat as "deadly serious". "We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out," he told reporters. Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security. While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of [USN:L1N44I06W TEXT:"calling for the assassination"] of senior Polish politicians. In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an [USN:L1N3W206N TEXT:"assassination attempt"] on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

item.title: From theatre to streets, Gen Z protester Neha Bora a new face of India's youth unrest
item.description: The 29-year-old doctoral student said she did not set out to become an activist.
item.dc:creator: Aftab Ahmed, Saurabh Sharma
item.content:encoded: A little-known doctoral student has emerged as one of the most visible faces of a protest movement in India that has mounted the most serious challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government in years. Neha Bora, 29, is one of a number of prominent activists detained this weekend as the authorities cracked down on attempts by protesters led by the "Cockroach" youth movement to demonstrate against what they say is massive vote-rigging to help Modi's party. But Bora, national president of the left-wing All India Students’ Association, says she did not set out to become an activist. She traces her path into politics to theatre and, later, the student-led protests against a citizenship law in 2019 and 2020. BORA URGES PROTESTERS ON FROM DETENTION On Saturday, after police blocked demonstrators from reaching New Delhi's designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, Bora urged them to regroup at Dilli Haat, a crafts market 10 km (6 miles) away. "Dilli Haat becomes Jantar Mantar today," she wrote on X before setting off towards the site, chanting slogans as others followed. Police detained her with several other activists. But even in detention, she called for the demonstration to continue. "I am in detention. The movement is not," she said in a video posted online, urging supporters who were stopped by police to protest wherever they were. She was released later on Saturday. The Cockroach Janta Party-led protests seek the ouster of India's election chief, claiming irregularities in handling voter data have led to the deletion of 130 million names — more than the population of Japan — from electoral rolls. The Election Commission denies favouring any group, and Modi's Hindu nationalist party has accused opponents of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Other issues Bora has championed include school-examination scandals, unemployment and police actions. Soft-spoken in conversation but forceful behind a microphone, she has built a following through speeches in Hindi and English, often invoking constitutional rights and linking student grievances to broader questions of inequality and government accountability. 'HOPE IS ALSO INFECTIOUS' Bora grew up in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand and moved frequently as a child because her father served in the army. She studied at Delhi University before beginning a doctorate at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics. As an undergraduate, she told Reuters in an interview this month, she joined a theatre group, where she learned to inhabit the lives of people much different from herself. "There might be a character that if you meet in your real life, you will disagree with, you will not like. But to do theatre is to understand where that person comes from." A turning point was the citizenship law, which critics say discriminates against Muslims. Bora said she watched students of her own generation lead classmates out of lecture halls and onto the streets, turning ideas she had encountered in books, films and documentaries into political action. She gained wider attention during protests in July over alleged leaks of exam papers, when she joined other activists in demanding the resignation of the education minister. Her speeches at Jantar Mantar, criticising the government and police response to demonstrators, circulated widely online. Bora has since become a fixture at demonstrations in the capital. During protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, she was repeatedly detained and returned to the streets after her release. She said ideology alone does not drive the current mobilisation, describing hope as a more powerful force. "Fear is infectious, of course. But hope is also infectious," she said. "People have courage now because they think that they can have courage." Bora said the demonstrations reflect the accumulation of years of grievances. "People remember," she said. "People carry that discontent, people carry that betrayal, people carry that disappointment."

item.title: Imran Khan's provincial government suspended by Pakistan president over militancy fight
item.description: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.
item.dc:creator: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy. The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency. The provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months. The move comes after Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party rallied for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to [USN:L8N45R072 TEXT:"march on the capital"] Islamabad in coming days amid deepening political instability. The federal government and the military have accused Khan's party of failing to curb Islamist militants in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, which has suffered an increasing number of [USN:L1N43Z03Y TEXT:"militant attacks"] in recent months. Khan's party rejects the allegation, saying the federal government failed to provide the provincial government with funding and equipment to combat the militancy. "The situation is so grave that you wouldn't see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Islamabad accuses neighbouring Afghanistan of harboring Islamist militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says that Khan's party had been sympathizing with both the Taliban in Kabul and their affiliates at home. Both the Afghan Taliban and Khan's party have denied the accusation. President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif following a federal cabinet decision, the president's office said. "This is more of a coup disguised as emergency," said Zulfikar Bukhari, Khan's aide and his party's spokesperson. Bukhari said it was a "ridiculous decision" that would only lead to further bloodshed and instability. The country's powerful military is widely seen as the ultimate power broker to decide who will rule the South Asian nation of 240 million. Khan's supporters say the military rigged the 2024 election against the 74-year-old former cricket star, an allegation the military denies. KHAN'S PARTY CHIEF MINISTER'S MOVEMENT BLOCKED Ahead of the planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists in recent days. Restrictions have been placed on Chief Minister, Sohail Afridi of Khan's party in the northwestern province, one of his close aides told Reuters. All roads leading to his office had been blocked with shipping containers, with hundreds of police deployed, said witnesses. The PTI's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces. The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said. STANDOFF OVER KHAN'S HEALTH The standoff comes more than a month after the government defied a court order and refused to allow Khan's treatment in a private hospital, despite mounting concerns over [USN:FWN44F00T TEXT:"his health"]. The protest also coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters. Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. He says he is a political prisoner and the military is making up charges to keep him out of the country's politics, a charge the army denies. Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violent attacks on military and state installations, and an accusation of an unlawful marriage. All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.

item.title: Bezzecchi pips Fernandez to win Indonesian GP, Martin retakes championship lead
item.description: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez. [USN:L4N45W00O TEXT:"Polesitter Fernandez"], racing with fractured fingers sustained in a crash on Saturday, looked untroubled in the opening half of the race as he and Bezzecchi surged away from the chasing pack. But the Trackhouse rider began to fade as the afternoon wore on, and a determined Bezzecchi finally pounced with nine laps remaining to seize the lead and secure victory, with Martin completing a podium lockout for Italian manufacturer Aprilia. Bezzecchi's win, the 300th victory for an Italian in MotoGP, also kept his faint championship hopes alive. "I'm very, very happy to be back on the top step of the podium," said the 27-year-old, who led the standings in the early stages of the season but has struggled in recent weeks. "It was a nice, nice battle with Raul. I think we deserve a result like this, me and all my team, especially them, because they never stop working. They've been through tough times with me." A dejected Fernandez revealed the full extent of his injury after the race. "Yesterday, when I crashed and I saw my hand, I knew before going to the clinic that I had my finger broken, the one that normally I used to brake," the Spaniard said. "This morning, when I woke up, I realised I don't have one, but two fingers broken. No one knew. I tried to say nothing, just keep the pain for me and keep my focus on the race. "This morning, I tried find a solution on the brakes, because I was not able to use the finger that I use normally. I started everything from zero. It was a very difficult job for me." MARTIN BACK AT THE TOP The most exciting duel in the race took place behind the top three, with Marquez engaging in a thrilling back-and-forth with KTM's Pedro Acosta. Marquez had a strong start and swooped into third place in the opening lap, but his Ducati struggled to keep pace with the Aprilia machines around him, and a hard-charging Martin picked him off with ease in the third lap. The defending champion was then quickly overtaken by Acosta, but for the second time in as many days, Marquez profited from tyre pressure issues for his opponent and was allowed back into fourth. When Acosta was sure he would not receive a penalty, he once again locked horns with Marquez, but as they traded blows, Trackhouse's Ai Ogura capitalised and moved past both riders to seal a first-ever 1-2-3-4 finish for Aprilia. Martin, the 2024 champion, moved up to 355 points at the top of the championship standings, with [USN:L1N45W01V TEXT:"Saturday's sprint-winner Marquez"] on 353 points after finishing in sixth place - the first time he has completed a full race at the Mandalika circuit. "The last few laps, I was struggling a lot with the tyres, physical condition, but I was able to finish on the podium, so really, really happy," Martin said. "We are still in the fight. We are still in the lead. It will be a tough championship, but I will give my all."

item.title: Hurricanes aim to extend win streak to 5, add to Flyers' woes
item.description: Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions. The Hurricanes aim for their fifth straight victory Sunday when they visit the winless Flyers for the second consecutive weekend. Carolina lost its first two games before posting a 3-2 triumph in Philadelphia on Oct. 3. Former Flyer Shayne Gostisbehere scored the overtime winner for the Hurricanes, who used that victory as a springboard to three more wins. Most recently, Carolina posted a 5-2 road victory over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday. Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook each registered a goal and an assist for the Hurricanes. "Every single line is contributing," Martinook said. "The 'D' is playing some of the best hockey I've ever seen the group play together. ... It's been fun to watch." Sebastian Aho added a shorthanded goal for his team-leading fifth goal, while Mark Jankowski and Taylor Hall also scored for the defending Stanley Cup champions. "We've definitely, after the first couple games, gotten into our game," Aho said. "Just playing Hurricanes hockey, and that usually gives you a chance to win." The Hurricanes have scored 21 goals during their four-game winning streak. Jankowski has scored in each of the last three games, while Brandon Bussi has earned the victory in each of his last two starts. "It was a good effort from pretty much everyone," Carolina coach Rod Brind'Amour said. "I liked it. ... When we're going, you can tell we're in sync." Philadelphia, meanwhile, has lost 10 straight games dating back to its second-round playoff series against Carolina. The Hurricanes swept the Flyers last spring en route to winning the Stanley Cup, and the hangover has continued into the current campaign, as Philadelphia is 0-4-2. "It's not like we're not trying," said rookie forward Porter Martone, who scored the Flyers' goal in Saturday's 5-1 road loss to the Boston Bruins. "These guys in this group, we care. I think a lot of people from the outside think it's lack of effort, but everyone in this room is giving it their all. We don't like this. We're not having fun right now. We want to win." Philadelphia has been outshot by a wide margin and outscored 24-7 in its first six games. The Flyers scored only three goals while going 0-2-1 on their three-game road trip that ended Saturday. The last time the Flyers lost their first six games was in 2008-09, when the team began 0-3-3 before rallying to make the postseason. "You've got to stick together," said Philadelphia coach Rick Tocchet, whose team played Saturday without forward Travis Konecny and defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York. "We're at the bottom. We're in the muck right now. Hopefully, we get some healthy bodies back, but you've just got to stick together. There's no other answer. We've all been, in life, in a situation where you're in a foxhole and we need some people to sit in a foxhole and stick together." --Field Level Media

item.title: Saudi stocks slide after attack on Riyadh airport
item.description: Saudi stocks fell on Sunday, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed at least 12 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi stocks fell on Sunday, a day after an [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attack on Riyadh's international airport"] killed at least 12 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) dropped 1% with most of its constituents in negative territory, including top lender Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) , which was down 1%. Oil major Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) was down 0.6%. Despite missile attacks on Riyadh's airport this week, organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"will go ahead"] this month. President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis, widening a regional conflict that spilled over from the US-Israeli war with Iran. Riyadh, along with the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes against targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims. In Qatar, the index (.QSI) retreated 1%, with petrochemical maker Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA) declining 2.2%.

item.title: Rangers begin life without Igor Shesterkin vs. slumping Canucks
item.description: The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night. On Saturday, the Rangers found out Shesterkin's season was over, and his absence threatens to derail a promising start for a team coming off missing the playoffs for the past two seasons. Dylan Garand will step in as the 2021-22 Vezina Trophy winner's replacement for the time being, and the Rangers hope his promise in limited action translates to success in regular work starting Sunday night when they host the Vancouver Canucks. Shesterkin, 30, was injured when his right skate collided with the goal post while sliding into position to make a save with 11:40 remaining in the second period of Friday's 3-1 loss at Washington, which halted a four-game winning streak. Shesterkin's season is over after he was 3-1-0 with a 1.79 goals-against average. The Rangers are now counting on Garand, who is 3-1-1 with a 1.31 GAA in five career games. "You never want to see guys get injured, especially your best player in Igor," Garand, 24, told reporters at practice Saturday. "He means a lot to the guys in this room and a lot to me personally. ... I'm excited for the opportunity. Going to put my heart and soul on the line for these guys and this city every night and just try to help the team win." Garand began this season third on New York's depth chart and was exposed to waivers before getting claimed. He is being elevated because Joonas Korpisalo is out for at least four more weeks due to a lower-body injury. Garand's backup will be journeyman Spencer Martin, who made six appearances last season when Shesterkin was injured in January and went 1-3-0 with a 4.13 GAA. "A guy (Shesterkin) that means so much to our team," defenseman Adam Fox told reporters at practice Saturday. "Obviously, still processing that and you still feel terrible. Personally having dealt with injuries the past few years and him, too, it (stinks) when you're not able to be out there and help the team. He's such an important piece to this team. It's an opportunity for everyone else to step up." The Rangers are hoping Garand can help them open a season 4-0 at home for the first time since 2009-10 after outscoring Tampa Bay, Utah and the Islanders 14-5. Vancouver has allowed a league-leading 29 goals through its first six games, including 14 in a three-game skid against the Vegas Golden Knights, Carolina Hurricanes and New Jersey Devils. The Canucks have permitted 98 shots on goal in their past three games, and have allowed three power-play goals apiece in the past two games. "From a work ethic standpoint, it just needs to be much more difficult for teams to recover pucks and get to their sets," first-year coach Manny Malhotra said of Vancouver's penalty-killing woes. Last season, the Canucks had the NHL's worst penalty-kill percentage at 71.5%. "That's a couple games in a row where our penalty kill has to bear down and get those kills," Vancouver forward Brock Boeser said after taking a pair of penalties against the Devils. "We got to stay out of the box, myself included." --Field Level Media

item.title: Russia's Yandex says data centre in Vladimir area shut down after drone attack
item.description: Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Sunday that its infrastructure had been damaged in a drone attack, resulting in the complete shutdown of its data centre in the Vladimir region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Sunday that its infrastructure had been damaged in a drone attack, resulting in the complete shutdown of its data centre in the Vladimir region. No one was injured in the attack, but some of Yandex's services are currently unavailable to users, the company said. This is the third major data centre to have been taken out of action in the last few days. On Friday, Yandex, which is heavily involved in Russia's AI development and is sometimes called "Russia's Google", [USN:R4N45F01R TEXT:"said"] its data centre in the Kaluga region southwest of Moscow had been struck by Ukrainian drones and partly put out of action. A day earlier, a Ukrainian attack [USN:L1N45U04H TEXT:"shut down"] Yandex's data hub in Sasovo, southeast of Moscow, where two of the three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model are housed.
