item.title: Musk vows affordable Starlink in India days before Ambani's record Jio IPO
item.description: Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO. Jio Platforms, which owns the telecom arm, is targeting a [USN:L4N45V0VX TEXT:"valuation of $106 billion"] in the offering. Much like SpaceX-owned (SPCX.O) Starlink, Jio's own satellite venture is also awaiting final security clearance to launch. Cheap data is the playbook that built Jio in India, and the one Musk has used in markets [USN:L1N3KA0IB TEXT:"like Kenya"] to unsettle local telecom players. SpaceX now plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, [USN:L4N45V0TK TEXT:"starting in the US"]. Musk did not specify prices for India, where mobile data costs about 8 cents per gigabyte, among the lowest in the world. "Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable," he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday. "The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," Musk added. 'PRIME MINISTER AMBANI' The billionaire's remarks were the latest in a [USN:L4N45V0R8 TEXT:"series of X posts"] where he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's entry into one of the world's biggest internet markets to favour market leader Jio. The posts have marked a sharp turn for Musk, who has long enjoyed a warm public rapport with Modi. India's government has denied any bias in its approval process, noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink's and Jio's, are all awaiting final security clearance. Late on Friday, Musk taunted Ambani directly, addressing him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would "consider allowing Starlink to compete". Reliance has not responded to requests for comment on Musk's remarks.

item.title: インド、選管トップ辞任要求で厳戒続く 「ゴキブリ党」創設者ら釈放
item.description: [ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] - インドの首都ニューデリーは１１日、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める若者らの抗議活動が２日目を迎えるのを前に警戒が続いている。裁判所は、警察が前日拘束した若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」創設者アビジート・ディプケ氏ら幹部３人の釈放を命じた。

ニューデリーでは１０日、有権者名簿の見直しを巡り、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める数千人規模の抗議集会が予定されていた。当局は集会を阻止するため市中心部を封鎖。ディプケ氏らはデリーに到着した航空機から降りる際に拘束された。

ＣＪＰの法務責任者ラトナ・シン氏は、ディプケ氏らが今後１年間、治安を乱さないことを条件に釈放されたとＸに投稿した。ソーシャルメディアで著名な活動家ドルーブ・ラティ氏も拘束されていたが、内務省当局者によると、今後の抗議活動に参加しないことを条件に１１日未明に釈放された。

警察は１０日、２０００人以上を拘束。１１日も数千人の警察官や準軍事組織要員を市内各地に配置した。１０日に拘束された人の大半は同日夜までに釈放された。

野党やモディ政権の批判勢力は、抗議参加者に対する当局の対応は強権的だと批判。国連機関も平和的な集会の権利を保障するようインド当局に求めた。

インド外務省は１１日、国連の対応を批判し、声明は「インドの内政への不当な干渉だ」と反発した。

抗議活動では、有権者名簿の見直しがモディ首相の与党インド人民党（ＢＪＰ）に不当に有利に働いているとして、ギャネシュ・クマール選挙管理委員長の辞任を求めている。選管とＢＪＰはこうした指摘を否定している。

item.title: Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief
item.description: Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Asia

Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief

Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.

Security personnel are seen at a blocked road amid ongoing protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Sajjad Hussain)

NEW DELHI: New Delhi braced for a second day of youth protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief on Sunday (Oct 11), as a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders. Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) , and the other leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi. They were produced in front of a magistrate early on Sunday. "Condition - no breach of peace for one year," the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said in a post on X announcing their release.

Loading

Activist and social media influencer Dhruv Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.

Related:

Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder ahead of youth protest

India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest

Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up. Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said. Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled. India's foreign ministry said on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."

A man rides a scooter past shuttered shops in a deserted market, on the second day of a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Bhawika Chhabra)

MILLIONS OF NAMES REMOVED FROM ELECTORAL ROLL The protests are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years. Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems. The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party. Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Commuters cross a checkpoint as police officers stand guard on the second day of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Priyanshu Singh)

Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced. The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions. The cockroach party, which began as an online satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister. The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles, and said it would not stop until India's election system was reformed.

Related:

CNA Explains: What India’s ‘cockroach’ protests reveal about a generation under pressure

New Delhi under lockdown as police clamp down on protests, detain Cockroach Party founder

item.title: NHL roundup: Mitch Marner's OT goal vs. Kings keeps Knights rolling
item.description: Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas. With Scott Laughton in the penalty box for tripping Shea Theodore six seconds earlier, Marner snapped a wrist shot from the high slot past a screen by Mark Stone and beyond the glove of Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper for the game-winner and his second goal of the season. It was Marner's eighth career overtime winner and his first with the Golden Knights. Trevor Connelly scored a goal and assisted on the game-winner, while Stone had two assists for Vegas, which extended its winning streak to four games. Carter Hart made 26 saves for the Golden Knights, who leapfrogged the Edmonton Oilers to move back into first place in the Pacific Division. Artemi Panarin scored the lone goal for Los Angeles, which remains winless (0-2-2) under first-year head coach Peter Laviolette. The Kings also have opened a season with four consecutive losses for the first time in franchise history. Maple Leafs 6, Avalanche 3 William Nylander had two goals and three assists, Auston Matthews had two goals and two assists, and Toronto downed Colorado in Denver. Nylander's three assists and five points matched his career highs. Easton Cowan and Nick Blankenburg also scored, Nick Paul had two assists and Sergei Bobrovsky turned away 30 shots for the Maple Leafs. Nathan MacKinnon had two goals, Brock Nelson also scored and Mackenzie Blackwood had 17 saves for the Avalanche, who lost for the first time in three home games this season. Wild 4, Panthers 1 Kirill Kaprizov tallied his seventh career hat trick and added an assist, and Minnesota handed host Florida its first regulation loss of the season in Sunrise, Fla. Matt Boldy had the other Wild goal, on a wrist shot 53 seconds into the game. He also assisted on one of Kaprizov's tallies. Goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 of 30 shots to earn the victory as Minnesota ended a two-game winless skid. Matthew Tkachuk scored Florida's lone goal, off a rebound of his own shot in the second period. Goaltender Jacob Markstrom allowed three goals on 28 shots. Lightning 5, Islanders 3 Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as Tampa Bay claimed its fourth straight victory, beating host New York. Tied 3-all, Hagel rifled a shot past Ilya Sorokin (21 saves) with a long wrister for his second goal. He added an assist for a four-point night. Jake Guentzel tallied twice, and Nikita Kucherov and Max Crozier each had two assists. Goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots. Tony DeAngelo recorded a goal and an assist, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Brayden Schenn scored as the Islanders lost for the first time in three games on home ice. Bruins 5, Flyers 1 Capping a three-point effort, Fraser Minten's second goal of the season concluded a three-goal third period for Boston in a win over visiting Philadelphia. Pavel Zacha and Mason Lohrei scored to give Boston leads after the first two periods. Marat Khusnutdinov and Casey Mittelstadt also lit the lamp, while Minten and JJ Peterka each had two assists and Jeremy Swayman made 14 saves. Porter Martone scored a power-play goal and Dan Vladar (27 saves) took the loss for Philadelphia, which remains winless in six games this season. The Flyers were missing Travis Konecny (lower-body) and Cam York (upper-body) due to day-to-day injuries. Oilers 3, Sharks 1 Tristan Jarry made 19 saves as Edmonton skated to a win against host San Jose. Mattias Ekholm, Vasily Podkolzin and Alex Formenton scored while Connor McDavid increased his early-season points total to 13 with an assist for the Oilers, who have won four straight games since dropping their season opener to the Vancouver Canucks. Macklin Celebrini's first goal of the season was the lone score for the Sharks, who have dropped two of their last three. Celebrini, who missed two games with a lower-body injury, led San Jose with 21:59 of ice time and placed two shots on goal. Yaroslav Askarov made 17 saves. Canadiens 1, Red Wings 0 Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give host Montreal the win over Detroit. Because the game was scoreless after 65 minutes both goalies -- Jacob Fowler of Montreal and Detroit's Daniil Tarasov -- were credited with a shutout. Both made 30 saves and both picked up their second career shutout. There were chants from the Montreal crowd of "We want Larkin" at times when the Red Wings' Dylan Larkin was on the ice, but booed him during his shootout attempt. Larkin asked to be traded in the. Hurricanes 5, Blackhawks 2 Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook both scored once and added an assist, and visiting Carolina used a three-goal second period to beat slumping Chicago. Mark Jankowski, Sebastian Aho and Taylor Hall also scored for the Hurricanes, who have won four straight games. Goaltender Brandon Bussi made 24 saves and Mike Reilly collected two assists. Roman Kantserov, with his first NHL goal, and Oliver Moore replied for the Blackhawks, while goalie Spencer Knight made 34 saves. Chicago has just one win in six games to start the season. Mammoth 4, Sabres 1 Utah scored twice on its league-leading power play and routed host Buffalo. After Buffalo's Tage Thompson and Utah's Kailer Yamamoto traded goals in the first period, the Mammoth broke the game open with two goals in just over two minutes late in the middle frame. Karel Vejmelka made 23 saves in his third win of the season while Colten Ellis stopped 26 in the loss. Yamamoto, John Marino and offseason acquisition Anders Lee each recorded a goal and an assist in the win. Devils 4, Canucks 1 Nico Hischier scored twice on the power play, including his 200th career goal, and New Jersey rallied to beat Vancouver in Newark, N.J. Jake Allen made 20 saves in his 500th career game to get the win as the Devils snapped a two-game losing skid. Jesper Bratt had a goal and an assist, Jesper Boqvist also scored and Jack Hughes had two assists for the Devils, who finished with three goals on the power play to claim their second win of the season. Linus Karlsson had a goal while Leevi Merilainen and Kevin Lankinen combined to stop 33 shots for the Canucks, who suffered their third consecutive loss. Paul Cotter, the NHL's Third Star of the Week, was held pointless in his first game with the Canucks against his former team. Senators 3, Predators 2 (SO) Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as Ottawa rallied for a win over visiting Nashville. Tim Stutzle had a goal and an assist in regulation and scored in the second round of the shootout. Drake Batherson also scored for the Senators, while Ottawa goaltender Linus Ullmark stopped 16 shots. Ross Colton and Jonathan Marchessault scored first-period goals, and Ryan O'Reilly had a shootout goal for Nashville. Murray recorded 18 saves in his first start since the 2023-24 season, when he played for the Dallas Stars. Penguins 2, Stars 1 (SO) Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and host Pittsburgh edged Dallas. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby also tallied in the shootout for the Penguins while Seguin and Wyatt Johnston scored for the Stars. After Rakell's goal put Pittsburgh up, goalie Arturs Silovs deflected Mikko Rantanen's shot to end it. The Stars forced overtime when Tyler Seguin tied it 1-1 with 30 seconds left in regulation. Jake Oettinger made 19 saves. Connor Dewar scored his first goal of the season for the Penguins. Silovs made 24 saves to earn the victory. Blues 5, Blue Jackets 3 Jimmy Snuggerud scored two second-period goals in quick succession and Jonatan Berggren scored the game-winning goal to help St. Louis halt its three-game slide with a home win over Columbus. The Blues entered the matchup buried in offensive woes during their three-game losing skid but found their flow as Jake Neighbours and Pavel Buchnevich also found the back of the net and Dylan Holloway picked up three assists. Jordan Binnington made 20 saves as he recorded his first victory of the season. Cole Sillinger, Kent Johnson, and Valeri Nichushkin lit the lamp for the Blue Jackets, while Jet Greaves finished with 22 saves. Ducks 4, Flames 2 Ryan Poehling broke a third-period tie and added an assist to pace visiting past winless Calgary. Frank Vatrano, Jackson LaCombe and Nikita Nesterenko also scored, and Mikael Granlund had two assists for the Ducks, who have won four of their first five games. Goaltender Ville Husso made 27 saves in his first start of the season for the win. Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev each scored, and Matt Coronato collected two assists for the Flames, who have lost their first five games in the worst start in franchise history and are the only without a point this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: World Bank in talks with dozens of countries about crisis aid, Banga says
item.description: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview. Banga said the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial [USN:S0N3XA08Z TEXT:"$25 billion in crisis funds"] that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February. However, a sharp spike in diesel and fertilizer prices and other factors, including the looming super El Niño weather effect, were adding to challenges facing developing countries, Banga said in an interview ahead of this week's annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. "There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion," Banga said, referring to the initial $25 billion plus another $35 billion that countries could tap by diverting resources from already approved World Bank projects. "We'll see, but we're ready. We're engaged. We're having conversations with a number of them, you know, 30 to 40 countries are in dialogue with us," he said. Many developing countries have been hit hard by the spike in energy prices and high interest rates that have increased borrowing costs at a time when their fiscal coffers are still depleted by measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic and the spike in inflation following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. World Bank estimates show that developing countries owe external creditors about $400 billion in 2026, with interest payments alone comprising one-third of the total. Banga said more countries had shown interest in retooling existing projects than in tapping the immediate crisis window to address their liquidity needs. If the situation worsened, the Bank could make available as much as $100 billion in funds, he said, exceeding the $70 billion disbursed during the pandemic. The World Bank last month announced that it attracted a [USN:L1N4580ZW TEXT:"record $112 billion in private capital"] in the year ended June versus $69 billion a year earlier, and more than triple the 2022 total before Banga, a former Mastercard CEO, became president. That was on top of the $123 billion invested from the bank's own resources for that year, for a combined $235 billion, Banga said, underscoring the importance of tapping all available resources, especially at a time when Western countries have sharply cut official bilateral development aid. "There is no one answer that fits when the world has these kinds of issues. What you need to do is figure out how to cut your coat to suit your cloth," Banga said. Banga said he expected further gains in private capital flows in coming years, aided by expanded political risk guarantees from the bank's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, growth in local currency financing, and continued work on regulatory reforms that made it easier for foreign investors. The private capital jump was biggest in projects in upper-middle-income countries like Argentina or India, which accounted for $50 billion of the private capital, and lower-middle-income countries including Bangladesh and Angola, which accounted for $37 billion. But more work was needed to boost the roughly $3 billion in private capital flowing to low-income countries. "In the smaller countries, it hasn't multiplied enough, and there are challenges," he said, noting the bank would announce some new initiatives this week aimed at ensuring micro-, small- and medium-sized businesses also had access to private capital. Banga said private capital growth was also regionally spread, with the largest increase seen in Latin America and the Caribbean, which accounted for $36.3 billion of last year's total, followed by Europe and Central Asia with $21.3 billion, South Asia with $19.2 billion and Africa with $22 billion. The top 10 recipient countries were Brazil, India, Turkey, Romania, Nigeria, Argentina, South Africa, Bangladesh, Mexico and Chile, the Bank said. Banga said the World Bank and IMF were working together to address the high debt levels plaguing many developing countries through a series of initiatives, including efforts to boost countries' domestic revenue collections. The Bank had already set up some debt-for-development swaps for Angola and Ivory Coast, and a portfolio-based guarantee for Argentina, and was working on over a dozen more projects. "We've got 14 or 15 in the pipeline, helping them rotate out higher-priced old debt for newer-priced debt with our guarantees," with the difference then targeted at education, healthcare, water, or nature programs, he said.

item.title: 債務増大や金利上昇が焦点、世銀・ＩＭＦ総会12日から エネルギー供給に懸念
item.description:
Andrea Shalal
[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。
年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。

年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。 期間中には２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の財務相・中央銀行総裁会議も開かれる。イランとの戦争が８カ月目に入り、エネルギー高によるインフレや公的債務の増大が議論の中心になる見通し。

今年のＧ２０議長国を務める米国のベッセント財務長官は欠席し、財務省高官２人を派遣する。米政府当局者によると、国内で予定があるという。ウクライナ戦争や米国による国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）への制裁を巡って各国間の緊張が高まる中、ベッセント氏がＩＭＦ・世銀総会に加えてＧ２０会合も欠席することに、各国から不満が出る可能性がある。

世界銀行のアジェイ・バンガ総裁はロイターに、イランによるホルムズ海峡封鎖後も世界経済は懸念されたほど悪化していないものの、再び下押し圧力が強まっていると指摘した。

世界の石油供給の約２割が途絶し、軽油や肥料の価格が上昇。Ｇ７は軽油と原油計１億バレルを緊急備蓄から放出することで合意した。トランプ米大統領は１０日、ロシアから軽油の供給を受けることで合意したと発表し、対ロ制裁も一時的に免除する。この決定にはウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が強く反発した。

２月２８日の戦争開始以降、１０億バレルを超える石油が主に民間在庫から市場に放出されたが、業界幹部によると、世界市場に供給可能な在庫は減少しており、価格上昇への市場の脆弱性が増している。

バンガ氏は、エルニーニョ現象に加え、肥料価格やエネルギーコスト、債務問題が重なることが世界経済のリスクになるとして、今後数カ月に備え「一段と慎重になる必要がある」と述べた。ＩＭＦのゲオルギエワ専務理事も年次総会を前にした講演で「冬が来る」と警告した。

ＩＭＦは２０２６年の世界経済成長率を３％程度とする見通しを大きく変更しないもようだが、ウクライナや、イランの攻撃を受けエネルギー輸出が大幅に減少した湾岸諸国などは下方修正が予想される。

もう一つの大きな懸念は公的債務の増大だ。世界の公的債務は第２次世界大戦後で最高水準にあり、２０３０年までに世界の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）の１００％を超える見通し。新興国や低所得国では米金利上昇に伴う資本流出も重荷となっている。

途上国では利払い費が政府歳入の平均１０％をすでに超え、より高い金利での債務借り換えを迫られている。新型コロナ禍ではＧ２０が最貧国の債務返済猶予に動いたが、今回は同様の措置への機運は乏しい。

米シンクタンクのアトランティック・カウンシルで国際経済部門を統括するジョシュ・リプスキー氏は 、安全保障と国際金融の結び付きが一段と強まっていると指摘。地政学的危機が世界経済に急速に波及する中、政策当局は「もはや以前と同じ世界ではないことを認識しなければならない」と話す。

item.title: Kings C Maxime Raynaud exits preseason game with right knee injury
item.description: Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud sustained an apparently serious right knee injury in the second quarter of a preseason loss to the host Golden State Warriors on Saturday night in San Francisco.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud sustained an apparently serious right knee injury in the second quarter of a preseason loss to the host Golden State Warriors on Saturday night in San Francisco. Raynaud was hurt while setting a screen for teammate Darius Acuff Jr. on Warriors guard Stephen Curry with 2:32 before halftime. As they collided, the 7-foot-1 center yelled in pain and crumpled to the floor. He was examined by medical staff and eventually was helped up, put in a wheelchair and exited the court to the locker room. The second-year player got tests on the knee in Chase Center, including the X-ray room, at halftime. The Kings announced in the third quarter that he was out for the rest of the game with a right knee injury. Sacramento did not have an update on his injury after the game, which Golden State won 111-106. Raynaud, 23, told reporters he was set to undergo an MRI late Saturday and was seen leaving the arena on crutches, per reports. Raynaud collected 10 points, five rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes as a reserve on Saturday. He was 3-for-3 from the field, including 1-for-1 on 3-point attempts. Sacramento selected the native of Paris in the second round of the 2025 NBA Draft out of Stanford. As a rookie, Raynaud averaged 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 26.5 minutes in 74 games (56 starts). He was selected to the All-Rookie second team. --Field Level Media

item.title: América empata y es líder general del torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: América, el club más ganador del fútbol mexicano con 16 títulos, empató el sábado como local ante Monterrey por 1-1 y se ubicó como líder general del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: América, el club más ganador del fútbol mexicano con 16 títulos, empató el sábado como local ante Monterrey por 1-1 y se ubicó como líder general del torneo Apertura. Con la igualada en la undécima jornada, las "Águilas" del América llegaron a 21 puntos en lo más alto de la tabla general, donde le siguen Toluca y Querétaro con 20 unidades. En el partido, disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, los "Rayados" de Monterrey se pusieron en ventaja a los 18 minutos con un vistoso remate de volea del uruguayo Diego Rossi en el área tras un preciso centro enviado por Orbelín Pineda desde el sector derecho. América empató en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte cuando el defensa uruguayo Santiago Bueno definió de derecha en el área chica después de que el portero argentino Estebán Andrada rechazó un remate de Henry Martín. En la segunda parte, ambos equipos salieron en busca del triunfo, generando llegadas de peligro en las dos áreas que no concretaron. América estuvo cerca de dar la vuelta al marcador a los 79 minutos con un potente disparo del colombiano Miguel Borja que se estrelló en el travesaño. El delantero colombiano fue expulsado a los 87 minutos tras cometer una fuerte falta sobre el defensa Carlos Salcedo. En los otros partidos del sábado, Querétaro ganó 2-0 al Atlante con goles del uruguayo Santiago Homenchenko y Denilson Muñoz. Atlas y Guadalajara empataron 1-1. Para los "Rojinegros" del Atlas anotó el argentino Kevin Zenón, mientras que para las "Chivas" de Guadalajara lo hizo Ángel Sepúlveda. En tanto, Bravos de Ciudad Juárez y Tijuana empataron 1-1 con goles del brasileño Rodrigo Dourado y del marroquí naturalizado español Mourad Daoudi. La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Atlético de San Luis juegue ante Santos Laguna, Pachuca enfrente a Necaxa y el vigente campeón Cruz Azul visite a Pumas UNAM. El viernes, Tigres UANL venció por 3-2 a Toluca, mientras que Puebla y León empataron 1-1.

item.title: Mitch Marner’s OT goal vs. Kings runs Golden Knights’ win streak to 4
item.description: Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas. With Scott Laughton in the penalty box for tripping Shea Theodore six seconds earlier, Marner snapped a wrist shot from the high slot past a screen by Mark Stone and beyond the glove of Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper for the game-winner and his second goal of the season. It was Marner's eighth career overtime winner and his first with the Golden Knights. Trevor Connelly scored a goal and assisted on the game-winner, while Stone had two assists for Vegas, which extended its winning streak to four games. Carter Hart made 26 saves for the Golden Knights, who leapfrogged the Edmonton Oilers to move back into first place in the Pacific Division. Artemi Panarin scored the lone goal for Los Angeles, which remains winless (0-2-2) under first-year head coach Peter Laviolette. The Kings also have opened a season with four consecutive losses for the first time in franchise history. Kuemper, who led the league with 15 losses in games decided beyond regulation last season, finished with 30 saves. Following a scoreless opening period, the teams exchanged goals in the second, which ended tied at 1 despite Vegas holding a commanding 14-3 edge in shots on goal. The Golden Knights took a 1-0 lead at 2:37 on a power-play goal by Connelly, who one-timed a cross-crease pass from Stone inside the right post for his second goal of the season. Los Angeles answered with a power-play goal by Panarin, who fired a shot from above the circles that sailed past a leaping screen by Alex Laferriere and caromed off the left post and in for his third goal. The Kings, who set an NHL record last season with 33 of their 82 regular-season games reaching overtime, fell to 0-2 in games decided beyond regulation this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Protesters seeking India election chief's ouster detained, as 'cockroach' leaders released
item.description: Youth protesters, many of them from student organizations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests around the city on Sunday afternoon before police hauled them away in vehicles.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Arpan Chaturvedi
item.content:encoded: Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for asecond day on Sunday as sporadic protests broke out demanding India's election chief quit, and a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders. [USN:L1N45W01X TEXT:"Dipke"] and the other Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi. The court ordered their release with an undertaking to "maintain public peace", the CJP said in a statement. "Cockroaches never die," the group posted on its X account shortly after Dipke's release. Youth protesters, many of them from students organisations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests around the city on Sunday afternoon before police detained them and hauled them away in vehicles. The All India Students' Association alleged in a post on X that those detained were assaulted by police inside the vehicles. A video posted on X by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) showed one of its lawmakers, John Brittas, being helped from a bus to an autorickshaw as he appeared to be in distress. Reuters could not verify claims about detainees being assaulted by police. The Delhi Police spokesperson did not respond to calls made by Reuters to seek comment. The youth movement is one of the biggest political challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his 12 years in power, during which his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has repeatedly swept the polls and eliminated any serious challenge by opponents, including the Congress Party. The protesters are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi.

item.title: Ducks stay hot, send Flames to worst start in team history
item.description: Ryan Poehling broke a third-period tie and added an assist to pace the visiting Anaheim Ducks to a 4-2 victory over the winless Calgary Flames on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ryan Poehling broke a third-period tie and added an assist to pace the visiting Anaheim Ducks to a 4-2 victory over the winless Calgary Flames on Saturday. Frank Vatrano, Jackson LaCombe and Nikita Nesterenko also scored, and Mikael Granlund had two assists for the Ducks, who have won four of their first five games. Goaltender Ville Husso made 27 saves in his first start of the season. Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev each scored, and Matt Coronato collected two assists for the Flames, who have lost their first five games in the worst start in franchise history. Goalie Dustin Wolf stopped 24 shots for Calgary, the only NHL team without a point this season. The score was tied 2-2 when Poehling gave the Ducks their third lead. While short-handed, he slid a shot along the ice past Wolf at 5:35 of the third period, converting on a rush. Poehling lost his footing when Calgary defenseman Zayne Parekh slid into him, sending him crashing into the net. Poehling slammed his knee into the post. After lying on the ice for an extended period, he was helped to the dressing room and did not return. Nesterenko provided an insurance goal with 2:57 remaining in regulation, chipping a loose puck into the net during a scramble. Until those goals, it was an even contest, perhaps even tilted in Calgary's favor. LaCombe opened the scoring midway through the first period, netting his first goal of the season by pouncing on a loose puck. Frost replied five minutes later with a quick-strike tally, finishing a rush up the ice by burying an open chance from the slot. Vatrano restored Anaheim's lead with 45 seconds remaining in the first period when he redirected a bouncing point shot into the net for his first goal of the season. Suniev again pulled Calgary even with 2:06 remaining in the second period. The 2023 third-round draft pick converted a sharp-angle shot for his first career NHL goal in his ninth game. The win came at a cost for the Ducks. Cutter Gauthier left the game after logging just 2:18 of ice time in the first period because of an upper-body injury and did not return. --Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Le Népal exhorte des villageois à évacuer après une inondation provoquée par un glissement de terrain
item.description: Les autorités népalaises ont exhorté dimanche des villageois à se mettre à l'abri après que plusieurs maisons et infrastructures ont été emportées par l'importante crue d'une rivière dans le centre du pays.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Les autorités népalaises ont exhorté dimanche des villageois à se mettre à l'abri après que plusieurs maisons et infrastructures ont été emportées par l'importante crue d'une rivière dans le centre du pays. Un glissement de terrain survenu dans le village de Chumnubri, dans la région de Gorkha, à environ 100 kilomètres à l'ouest de Katmandou, a obstrué la rivière Budhi Gandaki, provoquant des inondations en aval, ont indiqué les autorités. "Nous avons demandé aux villageois vivant le long des berges en aval de la rivière d'évacuer les lieux et de se mettre en sécurité", a déclaré Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, le plus haut fonctionnaire de la région de Gorkha. Dharmendra Kumar Mishra a indiqué que plusieurs maisons et deux ponts suspendus avaient été emportés, et qu'un projet hydroélectrique avait été endommagé par les inondations. Les autorités chargées de la gestion des catastrophes ont alerté les habitants vivant le long de la rivière dans les régions de Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi-Est et Nawalparasi-Ouest au sujet de cette crue. "Veuillez vous assurer que les personnes se trouvant dans les zones à risque soient évacuées à temps vers des lieux sûrs et apportez votre aide aux opérations de recherche et de sauvetage si nécessaire", a déclaré l'Autorité nationale de gestion des catastrophes dans un message publié sur les réseaux sociaux. Selon les responsables, des équipes de secours de l'armée et de la police ont été déployées sur place et surveillent également la situation. Des crues dévastatrices, provoquées par l'effondrement d'un glacier dans l'Himalaya, ont fait au mois d'août 1.457 morts au Népal et des milliers de personnes sont toujours portées disparues.

item.title: India unveils steel policy aiming for 604 million tons capacity by 2047
item.description: India released a draft steel policy for public consultation late on Saturday, targeting 604 million metric tons of steel capacity by 2047 from around 220 million tons at present.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India released a draft steel policy for public consultation late on Saturday, targeting 604 million metric tons of steel capacity by 2047 from around 220 million tons at present. Reuters reported last week, citing the draft document, that the policy [USN:L4N45L0E4 TEXT:"lays out plans"] to cut sector emissions and shore up access to iron ore and coking coal — key raw materials — to meet anticipated demand. The policy aims to cut the sector's average carbon-emission intensity to around 1.54 tons of carbon dioxide per ton of crude steel by 2047 from the current 2.54 tons, in line with India's net zero emission goal for 2070, according to the draft document. The steel ministry expects iron ore demand at 772 million tons and plans to secure access to high-grade reserves by pursuing foreign assets and joint ventures, the document said. The ministry also expects coking coal demand to reach 236 million tons, the document said, with the government planning to diversify its sourcing via "strategic global outreach" and acquire overseas assets.

item.title: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
item.description: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Thailand this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest energy supply shock ever and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Thailand this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest energy supply shock ever and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth. The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, being held outside of Washington for the first time in three years. Notably absent will be [USN:L1N45V0KM TEXT:"US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent"], who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handled some "domestic engagements," a US official said. His decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which the US leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine's battle against Russia's invasion and the US move to impose sanctions on the [USN:L8N45U28I TEXT:"International Criminal Court"]. World Bank President Ajay Banga told Reuters that while global growth had held up better than feared when Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, shutting off some 20% of the world's oil, pressures were building again. Soaring prices for diesel, rising fertilizer prices and a looming [USN:L6N44V0FF TEXT:""super" El Niño weather effect"] that experts say could lead to 450,000 heat-related deaths are all hitting at once. Group of Seven countries have agreed to [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"release 100 million barrels of diesel"] and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower gasoline prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"US sanctions"] designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of the war on February 28, but industry executives say the [USN:L6N45S103 TEXT:"amount of oil in storage"] that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fueling pressure on prices. Banga said the Bank was not revising down its global forecasts at the moment, but was keeping a close eye on developments. "The real thing is not just El Niño by itself; it's the combination ... What's happening to fertilizer prices? What's happening to energy costs? What's happening to debt? It's that put together that creates its own challenges," he said. "And I think that will call upon all of us to be far more careful on what we prepare for in the coming months." RISING DEBT IMF Managing Director [USN:L1N45S0Z3 TEXT:"Kristalina Georgieva"] issued a similar warning in her traditional curtain-raiser speech previewing the meetings, telling the audience, "Winter is coming." The IMF has signaled little change in its forecast for 3% global growth in 2026 and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher. But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia's invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports. IMF research released on Tuesday showed that [USN:L1N45R02Q TEXT:"sharp spikes in food and energy prices"] are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. One huge headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030. Advanced economies, led by the United States, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, El Niño, and lack of investment in AI, which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries. EMERGING MARKET CONCERNS Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Interest payments already exceed 10% of revenue in developing countries on average. Early in the COVID crisis, G20 leaders announced a suspension of debt service payments for the poorest countries, but there is little appetite for such action now, according to diplomats from G20 countries, who said high debt levels and political pressures posed bigger hurdles this time. Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programs that call for fewer, but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures. "Countries are already cutting their expenditures because their debt payments are going high and because of the IMF conditionality," said Iolanda Fresnillo, who works on debt justice for Eurodad. "We fear that this review of conditionality policy is just going to make things worse." Kenya, she said, had avoided a debt restructuring by cutting public expenditures and trying to raise taxes, but the changes sparked significant protests, especially by the young. The IMF risked losing credibility unless it acknowledged the severity of the crisis facing many developing countries. "As long as they continue with the governance structure that they have, they are becoming less and less relevant," she said. SECURITY AND FINANCE Flight routes to Bangkok often route through the Middle East, posing immediate security challenges to the 10,000-plus travelers descending on Thailand's bustling capital city of 9 million residents following recent [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attacks on Saudi airports"]. The last off-site annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank took place in Morocco just days after militants led by [USN:L8N45S0ZS TEXT:"Hamas killed 1,200 people in Israel"], followed by Israel's bombardment of Gaza that killed more than 74,000 people and devastated cities throughout the Palestinian area. Three years later, the linkage between national security and international finance is clear, although finance officials at the time had dismissed the Hamas attack as not being an economic issue, said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council. "Obviously there have been massive global ramifications," he said. "What we're currently experiencing with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has a direct connection with what happened three years ago." Policymakers needed to become more agile in responding to geopolitical crises in an increasingly interconnected world, Lipsky said. "They have to be proactive and they have to recognize that they don't live in the world they used to."

item.title: Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide
item.description: Authorities said several houses and two suspension bridges had been swept away, and a hydroelectric project was damaged by the flood.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide

Authorities said several houses and two suspension bridges had been swept away, and a hydroelectric project was damaged by the flood.

A Nepal national flag is seen in Devighat, Nuwakot district, Nepal on Sep 9, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Tyrone Siu)

FAST

KATHMANDU: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday (Oct 11) to move to safer places after a massive flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties. A dry landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100km west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said. The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing. "We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.

Mishra said about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges had been swept away, and a hydroelectric project was damaged by the flood. The flooded river carrying muddy sludge is rising and has washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. The army rescued six people from Jagat who were facing the risk of a landslide, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post. Another 18 workers at the hydroelectric project that had its camp was damaged escaped to safety, Uprety said. National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood. "Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post. Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

item.title: New Zealand pick Allen, Ferguson, Seifert for India ODIs, Ravindra returns
item.description: Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert will return to New Zealand's one-day international (ODI) squad for next month's home series against India, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert will return to New Zealand's one-day international (ODI) squad for next month's home series against India, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Sunday. Neither batter Allen nor fast bowler Ferguson have played a 50-over match for New Zealand since 2023, while Seifert's last ODI outing came in 2025. All-rounder Rachin Ravindra, who [USN:L6N45B019 TEXT:"dislocated his right shoulder"] during a promotional shoot last month, returns to the squad after he was [USN:L6N45B019 TEXT:"ruled out of the Twenty20 series"] beginning on October 22. "We're incredibly lucky to have the depth that we do to have 21 players involved in the series," head coach Rob Walter said in a statement. "It's also great to bring guys like Lockie, Finn, and Tim back into the one day unit. They're all exciting and explosive players in their own right and are proven match winners." New Zealand, who host India in five T20s, five ODIs and two tests, have named two separate squads for the first three ODIs and the final two matches. Seven additional players will join the squad after the third ODI in Hamilton on November 10, with a portion of the group departing to begin preparations for the test series. "With the ODI World Cup just one year away it's important for us to also view these matches as valuable preparation for that event," Walter added. "Bringing in seven players for the final ODIs allows us to test our depth and see how those players fare against a world-class side. "Obviously every test match is important for us in terms of championship points, which is why we're extracting some of that squad early for additional preparation before the first test." SQUAD FOR FIRST THREE ODIS Mitchell Santner (captain), Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Nathan Smith, Will Young, Blair Tickner SQUAD FOR FOURTH AND FIFTH ODI Mitchell Santner (captain), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Lockie Ferguson, Mitch Hay, Nick Kelly, Tim Seifert, Blair Tickner, Will Young

item.title: サッカー＝ロナルドに暫定的な出場停止処分、代表途中離脱で
item.description: ［１０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１０日　ロイター］　 - ポルトガル・サッカー連盟（ＦＰＦ）は１０日、代表合宿中に突如離脱した主将クリスティアノ・ロナルド（４１）に対して懲戒手続きを開始し、暫定的に出場停止処分を科したと発表した。

ロナルドは９月３０日に、欧州ネーションズリーグの試合に向けて遠征中の代表チームから離脱した。その後公開した長文の声明で、コンディション管理のため欠場予定だったノルウェー戦での起用を巡り、ジョルジェ・ジェズス監督は「約束を破った」とコメント。同監督は記者会見で事の経緯を説明すると合意していたものの、実際に話した内容は異なっており、「監督が私との約束を破ったのはこれが２回目だった」と述べていた。

ジェズス監督は、そのような合意はなかったと否定している。

ロナルドは同じ声明の中で合宿地を突然去ったことなどを謝罪し、ＦＰＦの処分を受け入れる意向を示していた。同連盟の規定では、代表チームでの活動を「放棄」した場合は１カ月から６カ月の出場停止処分を科すことになっている。

同選手はすでに所属クラブのアルナスル（サウジアラビア）に戻っており、９日の試合でゴールを決めている。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝Ｗソックスが地区シリーズ敗退、村上は最終戦で4三振
item.description: ［１０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１０日　ロイター］　 - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１０日、ア・リーグの地区シリーズ（５回戦制）第５戦を行い、村上宗隆内野手が所属するホワイトソックスはガーディアンズに０─２で敗戦。２連勝の後の３連敗で敗退した。

ホワイトソックスは四回に先発のショーン・バーク投手がガーディアンズの２番ホセ・ラミレス三塁手に先制２ランを打たれ、これが決勝打となった。村上は「４番・一塁」で出場し、４打数ノーヒット、４三振だった。

ガーディアンズの先発ギャビン・ウィリアムズ投手が５回２／３、１安打無失点、１２奪三振の好投で勝利投手となった。同投手は２日前に行われた第４戦では九回途中からリリーフ登板。１８球を投げてチームの勝利に貢献していた。

ＭＬＢ公式サイトによると、ポストシーズンの５回戦制のシリーズで２連敗の後、３連勝したのは２０１７年のヤンキース以来で、メジャー史上１１チーム目。

ガーディアンズは１２日から始まるア・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）でレイズと対戦する。その前日に開幕するナ・リーグの同シリーズでは大谷翔平選手、山本由伸投手、佐々木朗希投手が所属するドジャースがブルワーズと戦う。

item.title: Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide, 5 missing
item.description: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties. Two women and three men were out of contact, the national disaster authority said. The army said a further 49 people, including a foreigner, had been rescued. They did not give the person's nationality. A landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said. The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing. "We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat. The flood swept away about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said. The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority. National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood. "Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post. Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

item.title: 韓国コンテナ船、北極海航路で初の欧州往復 定期運航へ課題も
item.description:
Joyce Lee
[ソウル １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Joyce Lee

[ソウル １１日 ロイター] - 韓国のコンテナ船が１１日、北極海航路で欧州を往復する同国初の商業航海を終え、南東部の釜山港に帰港した。韓国政府は北極海航路の活用を進め、釜山を世界的な海運拠点に育てたい考え。

コンテナ船「パンスタ・アクロ」は８月２２日に釜山を出港し、５０日ぶりに帰港した。韓国当局によると、北極海航路なら通常のルートに比べて航海日数を約３分の１短縮できる可能性がある。李在明大統領は北極海航路の開拓を重点政策に位置付けており、政府は２０３０年までの定期運航開始を目指している。

ただ、航路はロシアの北極圏沿岸を通るため、ウクライナでの戦争を巡りロシアの孤立化を図る西側諸国との摩擦につながる可能性もある。韓国は今回の航海に先立ち、船が氷に閉じ込められた場合などの支援についてロシア側と協議した。

パンスタ・アクロは往路で北極海を通過し、欧州で最初の寄港地となる英国のフェリックストーに到着。その後、ロッテルダムとグダニスクに寄港し、再び北極海を通って帰国した。

今回の航海は商業化に向けた課題も浮き彫りになった。運航会社は出港前、約１３００ＴＥＵ（２０フィート換算のコンテナ数）の貨物確保を目指しているとロイターに説明していたが、実際に積載した貨物は７３７ＴＥＵにとどまった。

item.title: Chinese Apple supplier Luxshare sees little negative impact from US patent infringement probe
item.description: Chinese Apple supplier Luxshare Precision Industry said it expected little negative impact from a newly launched US patent infringement investigation, and the company was actively working to respond and protect shareholder interests.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese Apple supplier Luxshare Precision Industry (002475.SZ) said it expected little negative impact from a newly launched US patent infringement investigation, and the company was actively working to respond and protect shareholder interests. Below are the details based on Luxshare's exchange filing published late on Saturday. Luxshare said the US International Trade Commission (ITC) on October 9 launched a Section 337 investigation into the company and its subsidiary Dongguan Luxshare Technology over patent infringement claims brought by US company Vicor Corp. The probe, which is still in its preliminary stage, is focused on vertical power delivery systems, related components and computing systems containing them, and the ITC has not made any substantive findings, the Chinese company said. Luxshare said the affected products — used in power modules and power supply solutions for data centres — have not entered mass production, so the investigation was unlikely to have a material adverse impact on business operations or near-term results. Luxshare said it had begun studying the patents and products involved and was organising technical, legal and business teams to prepare a response. Luxshare said it would strengthen cooperation with clients and supply chain partners, and actively protect the interests of the company and shareholders.

item.title: Four All Blacks ruled out of second Wallabies test
item.description: Four New Zealand players have been ruled out of next weekend's second Bledisloe Cup test in Sydney following their comprehensive 50-19 victory over Australia at Eden Park, New Zealand Rugby said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four New Zealand players have been ruled out of next weekend's second Bledisloe Cup test in Sydney following their [USN:L1N45W02B TEXT:"comprehensive 50-19 victory"] over Australia at Eden Park, New Zealand Rugby said on Sunday. The All Blacks, who retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th straight year, will be without hooker Asafo Aumua and loose forward Anton Segner after both failed their second head-injury assessments Ethan Blackadder has picked up a calf injury, and wing Leroy Carter has been ruled out due to a "high ankle sprain", which he suffered while scoring a try in the second half. George Bell, Du'Plessis Kirifi, Anton Lienert-Brown and Jamie Hannah have been named as injury replacements Australia face their own personnel problems and will be without key centre Len Ikitau, who left Saturday's game in the first half with a head knock, while [USN:L4N45T0E6 TEXT:"Hunter Paisami"] has been suspended Jordan Petaia was also unavailable due to an ankle injury, with Corey Toole and Kadin Pritchard coming in as replacements

item.title: Guardians complete ALDS comeback, blank White Sox in Game 5
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Jose Ramirez hit a two-run homer and Gavin Williams struck out a franchise postseason-record-tying 12, leading the Cleveland Guardians to a 2-0 victory over the Chicago White Sox in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Jose Ramirez hit a two-run homer and Gavin Williams struck out a franchise postseason-record-tying 12, leading the Cleveland Guardians to a 2-0 victory over the Chicago White Sox in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night. Cleveland became the fourth team to win a best-of-five postseason series after losing the first two games at home. Erik Sabrowski, Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith joined Williams in a combined three-hitter for the Guardians, who will meet the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series starting Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla. "This was a difficult year, and for us to be one step away from the World Series, our ultimate goal, this is really exciting," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. Chicago struck out 21 times, the most in major league history for a nine-inning postseason game. That broke the record of 19 the White Sox set in their Game 3 loss on Wednesday. "We're all bummed and sad, knowing we probably should have got the job done," White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery said after the loss. Ramirez sent starter Sean Burke's knuckle curve 348 feet over the right-field wall, scoring Steven Kwan, who led off the fourth with the game's first hit. The 78 mph pitch was well below the strike zone, but Ramirez golfed it inside the foul pole, giving him seven RBIs over the final three games of the series. "Jose is Jose, we all love him. He always has that one moment all the time," Williams said. "We know what he's going to do." "Obviously, it came down to one pitch to Ramirez," Burke added. "He's a really good player. He's probably going to be in the Hall of Fame some day. But it's frustrating." Williams (1-0) carried a no-hitter into the sixth -- two days after recording the final three outs in Game 4 -- before Kyle Teel laced a two-out single. Williams, who had hit Colson Montgomery to open the sixth, walked Miguel Vargas after Teel's hit. Sabrowski entered and struck out Munetaka Murakami to end the inning. Williams worked 5 2/3 innings, allowing one hit and walking two. The right-hander's 24 strikeouts over three appearances were one shy of the Division Series record set by Gerrit Cole of the Houston Astros in 2019. Williams matched the Cleveland single-game postseason record of 12 strikeouts, set by Charles Nagy in the 1996 ALDS against the Baltimore Orioles. Williams owns two of the five double-digit strikeout performances in team playoff history. "It's pretty satisfying," Williams said. "No matter what point (of the postseason) it is, it's always fun. And just being able to celebrate with the guys, it's a dream come true." Burke (1-1) allowed two runs on four hits over five innings, striking out four. Smith, who pitched the final 1 2/3 innings for his first save of the postseason, and Gaddis appeared in all five games. "Our back end of the bullpen has been the lifeblood of this team since I've been here," Vogt said. "They have the highest leverage. They have the toughest outs to get. And Eric came in, you just felt like he was going to do what he did." --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: River Plate vence a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que sella su descenso en liga argentina
item.description: River Plate volvió al triunfo el sábado al vencer 1-0 como local a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que selló su descenso a la segunda división del fútbol argentino.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: River Plate volvió al triunfo el sábado al vencer 1-0 como local a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que selló su descenso a la segunda división del fútbol argentino. Con la victoria en la duodécima jornada del Torneo Clausura, River llegó a 16 puntos y se ubicó novenol en la tabla de posiciones de la Zona B, a dos unidades de los ocho puestos de clasificación a la postemporada. En el partido disputado en el estadio Monumental ante 85.000 aficionados, el gol lo anotó el defensor Marcos Acuña a los seis minutos de juego, tras un centro de Ángel Correa. "Fue una victoria importante. El equipo jugó un buen partido y logramos el triunfo, aunque no pudimos ampliar la diferencia y cerrar el partido", dijo el delantero Lautaro Pereyra a la televisión local. Por su parte, a falta de cuatro fechas para el final de la fase regular, Estudiantes se convirtió en el primer equipo en confirmar el descenso tras una campaña con dos victorias, cinco empates y 21 derrotas. "Peleamos todo el año, pero nunca pudimos hacer pie. Errores, mala suerte, y termina pasando lo que no queríamos un par de fechas antes", dijo el defensor de Estudiantes Gonzalo Maffini tras la derrota. En otros partidos del sábado, Barracas Central superó 2-0 como local a Huracán y Banfield ganó 2-1 en su visita a Tigre, mientras que Central Córdoba y Estudiantes de La Plata igualaron 2-2. El viernes, Boca Juniors igualó 2-2 ante Instituto de Córdoba, Defensa y Justicia venció 2-0 a Unión y Sarmiento superó 3-1 a Aldosivi, en tanto que Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata y Atlético Tucumán empataron 1-1.

item.title: WHO unsure what caused pneumonia that killed plague-lab worker in Russia
item.description: The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

WHO unsure what caused pneumonia that killed plague-lab worker in Russia

The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media.

A satellite image shows the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk, Russia, May 8, 2025. (Photo: Reuters via Handout Google/Airbus)

FAST

GENEVA: The World Health Organization (WHO) said on Saturday (Oct 10) that it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a Russian lab worker at an anti-plague research centre in Siberia this month, and that no case of plague had been registered. The WHO said the Russian state regulator reported that tests of the lab worker and those who came in contact with her were negative for the high-threat pathogens tested, that her contacts still showed no symptoms, and that no further linked cases of severe pneumonia had been identified. "Based on the information provided ... (the) WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event. A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker," it said in a statement. The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media. Global health officials have been extra alert to fatal pneumonia cases of undetermined cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading fatal respiratory illness in China. The cause of individual pneumonia cases can often not be determined. Russian authorities have said the lab worker was appropriately vaccinated and that they found no microorganisms linked to her work in her body. On Thursday, Russia said it had completed health checks on all the worker's contacts. It says it had provided full information to the WHO according to established procedures.

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝プレシーズンでクリッパーズ敗戦、八村14得点 河村10得点
item.description: ［１０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１０日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）、八村塁と河村勇輝が所属するクリッパーズは１０日、ラプターズとプレシーズンマッチを行い、１０６─１１４で敗れた。

八村は先発し、合計１８分３１秒プレー。３ポイントシュート３本中１本に成功し、チームトップの１４得点に加え、３リバウンド、１アシスト、１スチールをマークした。

チームメートの河村勇輝は控えとして合計１４分１５秒プレーし、こちらも３ポイント１本に成功して１０得点、４アシスト、２スチールを記録。クリッパーズはプレシーズンで１勝１敗となった。

クリッパーズは１４日、プレシーズン最終戦でナゲッツと対戦。２１日のキングス戦でシーズン開幕を迎える。

item.title: トランプ氏、ウクライナ大統領の交代求める 軽油高騰でロシア製油所攻撃を批判
item.description:
Max Hunder Steve Holland
[１０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Max Hunder　Steve Holland

[１０日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１０日、「ウクライナは新しい大統領を選ぶときだと思う」と述べ、ゼレンスキー大統領の交代を求めた。ウクライナによるロシアの製油所への攻撃が世界の軽油供給に打撃を与えていると批判した。

トランプ氏は前日、ロシアから軽油を輸入することで合意したと発表。ゼレンスキー氏は、合意がロシアを勢いづかせたと強く反発した。

米国とイスラエルが２月にイランを攻撃して以降、世界的に軽油価格が急騰しており、来月の米中間選挙を控えてトランプ氏の共和党にとって政治的な重荷となっている。選挙では野党・民主党が上下両院の一方、または両方で多数派を奪還する可能性がある。

トランプ氏が軽油供給合意を発表したのは、ウクライナと欧州の当局者が９日に米マイアミで米側と戦争終結に向けた共通案を協議している最中だった。ゼレンスキー氏によると、発表はウクライナ側にとって予想外だった。

英国のバーナム首相は１０日、ゼレンスキー氏と電話会談し、対ロシア制裁を強化する考えを伝えた。英首相官邸が明らかにした。両首脳は数日中に直接会談する予定という。

item.title: L'armée américaine met hors d'usage un navire dans le golfe d'Oman
item.description: L'armée américaine a déclaré samedi avoir mis hors d'usage un navire commercial dans le Golfe d'Oman après que l'équipage, ignorant des avertissements, a tenté de forcer le blocus naval imposé par les Etats-Unis contre l'Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'armée américaine a déclaré samedi avoir mis hors d'usage un navire commercial dans le Golfe d'Oman après que l'équipage, ignorant des avertissements, a tenté de forcer le blocus naval imposé par les Etats-Unis contre l'Iran. "Un avion de chasse de l'armée américaine a frappé la poupe du M/V Ocean Molica (également connu sous le nom d''Arika Sun'), battant pavillon panaméen, à l'aide d'une munition à guidage de précision, rendant ainsi le système de propulsion du navire totalement hors d'usage, sans blesser l'équipage", a indiqué le commandement central de l'armée américaine (Centcom) sur le réseau social X. Le Centcom a indiqué que le navire avait tenté de traverser les eaux régionales après avoir quitté un port iranien.

item.title: Canadiens blank Red Wings in rare 1-0 shootout victory
item.description: Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give the host Montreal Canadiens a 1-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give the host Montreal Canadiens a 1-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night. Jacob Fowler made 30 saves in regulation and overtime for the Canadiens, who snapped their three-game losing streak (0-2-1). Daniil Tarasov also stopped 30 shots in the first 65 minutes for the Red Wings, who dropped their second in two nights (0-1-1). It was the second career shutout for both goaltenders. The Canadiens had three goals called back. Alexandre Texier's apparent overtime winner 2:37 into the extra period was overturned by an offside challenge from Detroit coach Todd McLellan. Bolduc was offside. An apparent goal by Cole Caufield 1:16 into the game was reversed by video review because the puck did not completely cross the goal line. Bolduc put the puck into the net 7:05 into the second period, but the goal was immediately waved off because of goalie interference by Jake Evans. There were chants from the Montreal crowd of "We want Larkin" at times when the Red Wings' Dylan Larkin was on the ice, but booed him during his shootout attempt, which was stopped by Fowler. It was first reported on June 4, that Larkin asked to be traded and was removed as the team's captain at the beginning of training camp. Bolduc hit the goal post with 8:07 left in the first period. Fowler made a big save on Alex DeBrincat's wide-open backhand attempt from just below the left circle with a little less than five minutes remaining in the second period and stopped Andrew Copp on a breakaway attempt 3:37 into the third. Tarasov denied a shot that deflected off of Caufield just outside the crease at the 6:09 mark of the third period. Montreal defenseman Kaiden Guhle made his season debut after undergoing adductor muscle surgery over the summer. --Field Level

item.title: Brandon Hagel (hat trick), Lightning down Islanders for 4th straight win
item.description: Tampa Bay's Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as the Lightning claimed their fourth straight victory, beating the host New York Islanders 5-3 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tampa Bay's Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as the Lightning claimed their fourth straight victory, beating the host New York Islanders 5-3 on Saturday night. Tied 3-all, Hagel rifled a shot past Ilya Sorokin (21 saves) with a long wrister for his second goal and added his third into an empty net as Tampa Bay won the first of its two-game set in New York. He added an assist for a four-point night. Jake Guentzel tallied twice, and Nikita Kucherov and Max Crozier each had two assists. Goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots. Defenseman Tony DeAngelo recorded a goal and an assist, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Brayden Schenn scored as the Islanders lost for the first time in three games on home ice this season. New York forward Matias Maccelli had his 121st career assist in his 300th NHL game. A turnover led to the first goal as Pageau flipped a puck from the end boards out near the right circle in his defensive end. Guentzel gained possession and sent in an unassisted tally at 5:45 of the first period. Vasilevskiy kept the Islanders off the scoreboard by denying Bo Horvat on a breakaway after Tampa Bay defenseman Victor Hedman gave away the puck. Horvat fired a shot on the 1-on-1 try, but the Vezina Trophy winner turned it away at 11:14. A 36-goal scorer last season, Hagel watched Hedman backhand a long flip down the ice and used his speed to run it down. He beat defenseman Ryan Pulock to the puck and tallied at 15:42 for a two-goal lead through the opening period. Despite being banged up, New York's blue line put the club on the board in the second period when DeAngelo took a feed from Ondrej Palat and fired home his first goal from the deep slot at 6:27. Guentzel netted his second with his team on the power play. Kucherov found him to the left of Sorokin, and the winger made an inside move and beat the goalie for his third marker at 7:54 for a 3-1 advantage. Pageau made up for his earlier miscue to cut the Islanders' deficit to 3-2 at 11:41 of the second period. On Schaefer's deep shot, Pageau tipped it past Vasilevskiy. In the final moments of the second, Horvat helped tie it when his pass through the crease went in around a tangle of players near Vasilevskiy while the Islanders were on a power play. Schenn was credited with his second score of the season. Hagel broke the tie with 1:44 remaining in regulation, then completed his hat trick with an empty-net goal 21 seconds later to seal the victory. --Field Level Media

item.title: Senators rally from early 2-goal deficit, beat Predators in shootout
item.description: Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as the Ottawa Senators rallied for a 3-2 win over the visiting Nashville Predators on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as the Ottawa Senators rallied for a 3-2 win over the visiting Nashville Predators on Saturday. Tim Stutzle had a goal and an assist in regulation and scored in the second round of the shootout. Drake Batherson also scored for the Senators, while Ottawa goaltender Linus Ullmark stopped 16 shots. Ross Colton and Jonathan Marchessault scored first-period goals, and Ryan O'Reilly had a shootout goal for Nashville. Murray recorded 18 saves in his first start since the 2023-24 season, when he played for the Dallas Stars. Ullmark saved Steven Stamkos' final shootout attempt to secure the win. Earlier in the third, with an extra attacker on the ice, Stutzle's shot deflected off Pinto and ricocheted off Batherson's shin to tie the game at 2-2 at 18:37. The Predators struck first at 8:50 of the opening period when a loose puck emerged from a crowd near the left circle. Colton collected it and snapped a quick shot past Ullmark into the top-right corner of the net. Marchessault doubled Nashville's lead on the power play at 13:10. Taking a pass from Stamkos just below the left circle, Marchessault turned and fired, slipping a shot between Ullmark's stick and the post to make it 2-0. Ottawa cut its deficit to 2-1 on a power-play goal at 9:29 of the second period. Dylan Cozens slid a cross-ice pass to Stutzle, who rifled a one-timer into the net. Murray gloved Cozens' shot at 13:40 of the second period. Moments later, Thomas Chabot's wrist shot through traffic rang off the left post. Later in the second period, the Predators killed off Ottawa's 5-on-3 advantage. The Predators killed off a power play to open overtime, and as Roman Josi emerged from the penalty box, he collected a rebound at center ice and skated in alone on Ullmark, who turned aside his shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rickard Rakell lifts Penguins over Stars with shootout winner
item.description: Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and the Penguins beat the Dallas Stars 2-1 Saturday night in Pittsburgh.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and the Penguins beat the Dallas Stars 2-1 Saturday night in Pittsburgh. Dallas forced overtime when Tyler Seguin tied it 1-1 with 30 seconds left in regulation after Roope Hintz won a faceoff and Seguin deflected Jason Robertson's shot past Arturs Silovs. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby also tallied in the shootout for the Penguins while Seguin and Wyatt Johnston scored for Dallas. After Rakell's goal put Pittsburgh up, Silovs deflected Mikko Rantanen's shot to end it. Connor Dewar scored his first goal of the season for the Penguins, who were playing the second of a back-to-back and had lost three straight (0-2-1). Silovs made 24 saves. Jake Oettinger made 19 saves for Dallas, which had won two straight. Oettinger, who came in with consecutive shutouts, saw his shutout streak end at 188:52, the third longest in franchise history. Crosby is still looking for his first regulation goal six games into the season. Pittsburgh was 0-for-5 on the power play; Dallas was 0-for-3. The Penguins appeared to take a 1-0 lead late in the first period when Stars forward Justin Hryckowian tapped a loose puck into his own net during a scramble in front. But it was ruled that Pittsburgh's Hendrix Lapierre used a high stick earlier in the sequence. Silovs robbed Seguin with his left pad with 4:25 remaining in the second period to keep the game scoreless. Oettinger made a superb glove save against Crosby in the slot in the opening minute of the third period. Dewar made It 1-0 at 1:57 of the third period. He carried the puck into the zone along the left boards, cut across the slot and lifted a backhand that deflected off Dallas defenseman Lian Bichsel's stick and over Oettinger's right shoulder. Oettinger made a pair of saves on Evgeni Malkin in the final minute of overtime. --Field Level Media

item.title: サッカー＝バルセロナ快勝で開幕からの連勝キープ、レアルは辛勝
item.description: ［マドリード １０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マドリード　１０日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのスペイン１部は１０日、各地で試合を行い、昨季王者で首位のバルセロナがヘタフェを３─０で下し、開幕から８連勝とした。

バルセロナは前半２分、アンソニー・ゴードンの放ったシュートが相手選手に当たってコースが変わり、ネットを揺らして先制に成功。同３０分にはこの日が新天地での初先発となったガブリエル・ジェズスが加点し、最後はジュール・クンデのゴールで締めくくった。

レアル・マドリードはビリャレアルに１─０で辛勝。後半１７分に１９歳のヤン・ディオマンデがオフサイドトラップをかいくぐって挙げたゴールが決勝点となった。今夏に加入した同選手にとって、これがレアルでの初ゴール。

レアルはその８分後、ビニシウス・ジュニオールがネットを揺らすも、ビデオ・アシスタント・レフェリー（ＶＡＲ）の介入により、ゴール前に相手選手の髪を引っ張っていたとしてノーゴール判定に。さらにジュニオールは一発退場となった。

その他、アトレチコ・マドリードはアラベスに２─１で勝利。ラヨ・バリェカノ─ビルバオの一戦は、スタジアムでラヨのファンがクラブオーナーへの抗議としてピッチに物を投げ込むなどし、１５分間の中断の後に中止となった。

item.title: 米司法省、独禁法違反の疑いでテレビ5社調査 ホワイトハウス取材停止巡り
item.description:
[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - 米司法省は３日、ＡＢＣ、ＣＢＳ、ＣＮＮ、ＮＢＣ、ＦＯＸのテレビ局５社を反トラスト法（独占禁止法）違反の疑いで調査していると明らかにした。ＣＮＮなど３社の記者証を取り消したホワイトハウスに抗議し、各局が代表取材をボイコットしたことを受けた措置。
司法省の報道官は「ライバル企業同士が集団でボイコットすることは、シャーマン法に違反する可能性がある」と指摘。「反トラスト局は、これらの報道機関が反トラスト法に違反したかどうかを判断するため調査しているにすぎない」と述べた。
トランプ政権と主要報道機関の対立が相次ぐ中、今回の調査は新たな火種となる。トランプ大統領は主要メディアを繰り返し「フェイクニュース」と呼び、記者とのやり取りで衝突することも多い。
各社からコメントは得られていない。
ホワイトハウスは９月１９日、ＣＮＮ、ポリティコ、ＭＳ
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - 米司法省は３日、ＡＢＣ、ＣＢＳ、ＣＮＮ、ＮＢＣ、ＦＯＸのテレビ局５社を反トラスト法（独占禁止法）違反の疑いで調査していると明らかにした。ＣＮＮなど３社の記者証を取り消したホワイトハウスに抗議し、各局が代表取材をボイコットしたことを受けた措置。

司法省の報道官は「ライバル企業同士が集団でボイコットすることは、シャーマン法に違反する可能性がある」と指摘。「反トラスト局は、これらの報道機関が反トラスト法に違反したかどうかを判断するため調査しているにすぎない」と述べた。

トランプ政権と主要報道機関の対立が相次ぐ中、今回の調査は新たな火種となる。トランプ大統領は主要メディアを繰り返し「フェイクニュース」と呼び、記者とのやり取りで衝突することも多い。

各社からコメントは得られていない。

ホワイトハウスは９月１９日、ＣＮＮ、ポリティコ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷの記者証を取り消し、記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止した。ホワイトハウスは、大統領を取材することは「権利ではなく特権だ」と主張した。
